dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah. Excellent. This is exactly the kind of trickery I'm paying you for. But, but how do we turn your average Joe Sixpack against Mary Bailey?
Congratulations, Mr. Burns. The latest polls show you're up six points.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Giving me a total of...
With this team of investigators: your muckraker...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How do you do.
But first, there's a burning issue that we need to address and neutralize immediately.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I hate that fish!
There you go.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm going to be sore tomorrow.
But there's a downside to it. The latest polls indicate you're in danger of losing touch with the common man.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, dear. Heaven forefend.
Well, we've done all we can, Mr. Burns. The rest is up to you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, don't worry --
Which is why the night before the election, we want you to have dinner at the home of one of your workers.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh. I get your angle. Every Joe Meatball and Sally Housecoat in this God-forsaken state will see me hunkering down for chow with Eddie Punchclock. The media will have a field day!
Their job is to turn Mary Bailey from this...into this.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Visual aids help so much. Thank you.
Yes, we are. Come on boys, the old guy's finished.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait! Come back! You can't do this to me! I'm Charles Montgomery Burns!
The only question is -- can we find someone common enough...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I... I knew there would be sacrifices.

Hi-de-hi, Springfield! Dan Hoard, mikeside. Tonight -- our Isotopes take on the pesky Shelbyville Shelbyvillians. The 'Topes are looking to snap that darn twenty-six game losing streak, longest in professional baseball. How 'bout that? -- Our sleepy town is in the record book!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, sitting with the employees. I guess this proves I'm their friend. You did get me something on an aisle, Smithers? I don't want to be surrounded by them.
Bases loaded. 'Topes have one out, down by three. Here's the pitch. Swung on and missed! Strike three. Of course.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Damnation! These banjos couldn't carry Pie Traynor's glove.
Like this, Skip?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, you're a manager's dream, Strawberry.
Some of these guys have a bad attitude, skip.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: They sure do, Strawberry.
Sure do, Skip.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. Now, before I post the starting line-up I want to assure those of you whose names are not on the list, that I'm very disappointed in you. Something was lacking, let's call it heart.
You're pinch-hitting for me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. You see, you're a left-hander. And so is the pitcher. If I send up a right-handed batter, it's called playing the percentages. It's what smart managers do to win ballgames.
But I've got nine home runs today.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You should be very proud of yourself. Sit down! Simpson! You're batting for Strawberry.
You know sir, tipping is customary.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, me sorry, me no speaky Chiny.
Oh my God! And I just bought a boat!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, don't people answer the door these days?
Hold it right there. You're not leaving with that man. He's born again. Been baptized in a toilet sink.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Everyone doesn't have to know that part.
But I cleansed you of your evil!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I had a little left between my toes. It quickly multiplied, and now I'm a bigger bastard than ever. But I must know -- what was it about me that made you try?
And now your evil is gone!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm afraid that was just my pre-evil.
Feel his power!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've died and come back. It's overrated.
Welcome to the Lord, brother.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So that hellhole became my Heavenhole. I joined the prison choir...and the Prison Beatles Tribute Band.
Because I've killed so many rich white men, I thought I'd do right by at least one.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We're not so different, you and I.
Burns, you shall reject Satan!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why can't you reject your guy?
Comin' up, just sign here. Careful, hot pen.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm... Who's that goat-legged fellow? I like the cut of his jib.
Yeah, well, uh, she's alive, but... she's a nun.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Married to Jesus, eh? Does he beat her?
Jesus? No, he's a real Eagle Scout, that one. But your penguin's not a Catholic. She's a Buddhist nun. Spent her life expressing her sexuality with a Zen garden.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Those raked rocks could've been me! Now since you're so good at finding things, find the exit!
There is the little matter of my fee.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're becoming very tiresome.
Yes. I just need to erase your memory.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Attention, insects! The foot of reckoning has arrived!
In his ecstasy! Then off, off forth on swing!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Where's my bird going?!
Look, we just want to make movies. Not kill things.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes... that's the one. Smithers had thwarted my attempt to take candy from a baby, but with him out of the picture, I was free to wallow in my own crapulance.
All right, anyone else want to be a hero?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Marge, I'm giving you a raise and a new office... right next to mine.
Yep. It's time for the gold watch.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you. You are free to go.
Fine. I still like him better than Steinbrenner.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, you rag-tag bunch of misfits. You hate me, and I hate you even more. But without my beloved ringers, you're all I've got. So I want you to remember some inspiring things that someone else may have told you in the course of your lives, and go out there and win!
Look, Mr. Burns. I don't know what you think sideburns are, but...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Don't argue with me! Just get rid of them.
I hope she didn't take my attempt to destroy her too seriously.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Where's Homer? Oh, and to think I spent all afternoon baking him this cake.
And my good friend Frankenstein is now Frankenreagan. Bleh!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent. Now, to the matter at hand. Who will we put up for young Wilcox's congressional seat?
Hey, I think they liked us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Have the Rolling Stones killed.
I'VE SEEN HOW YOU SPARKLE / WHEN FALL NIPS THE AIR. / I KNOW YOU IN AUTUMN / AND I MUST BE THERE.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, nothing lifts my spirits like shopping.
Clear!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But wait, perhaps I'm being too hasty. You are highly skilled... at goofing off!
We're ready with the transfusion.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I'm not going to make it. I want to dictate... my epitaph.
I am that guy!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, we could make a fortune with these Bible pictures. And I've been looking for a way to launder the money I made selling club soda as flu vaccine.
But Mr. Mayor, these people have waited in line. And dogs can't even get the disease.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: They'll see me take it and they'll want some. Yes 'oo will. Yes 'oo will. You little jelly belly.
Now look, I'm the doctor here!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I demand a second opinion.
Oh yeah. Tons of it. Just say when.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A million dollars! Smithers! I want this Homer J. Simpson fired!
...so for the love of God, get me to Mexico!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hey, swabby. You've missed spots there... and another one there... and there... Every other spot is begrimed!
So, this is what successful post-op looks like!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Step right up, only two bits!
These pre-date stainless steel so you can't get them wet.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm, he's a worthy foe. Look at him, Smithers. Exercising away while the others are off at the candy machine.
Ey, what kind of woo hoo is this?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome to the most frustrating, befuddling, and yes, erotic, book release party you've ever attended.
Stee-rike!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: / SEE MY VEST, SEE MY VEST / MADE FROM REAL GORILLA CHEST / FEEL THIS SWEATER, THERE'S NO BETTER / THAN AUTHENTIC IRISH SETTER... / SEE THIS HAT, T'WAS MY CAT / MY EVENING WEAR, A VAMPIRE BAT / THESE WHITE SLIPPERS ARE ALBINO / AFRICAN ENDANGERED RHINO... / GRIZZLY BEAR UNDERWEAR / TURTLES NECKS, I'VE GOT MY SHARE / BERET OF POODLE ON MY NOODLE, / IT SHALL REST... / TRY MY RED ROBIN SUIT / IT COMES ONE BREAST OR TWO... / SEE MY VEST, SEE MY VEST, SEE MY VEST / / LIKE... MY... LOAFERS? / FORMER... GOPHERS... / IT WAS THAT OR / SKIN MY CHAUFFEURS
Just a minute.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who the devil are you?!
Oh, let's see, should I take the "Trail of Death," or the "Path of Doom?" Maybe I should just go back.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Is this Wall Street Journal online?
I don't care about the money. The whole monetary system is just a series of interconnected heterogeneous data bases.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Could you... repeat that first part?
Now, Burns, what if everything in town not powered by electricity were powered by electricity. The electricity you sell them. Imagine that.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My doctor says I'm not allowed to imagine. So I hired someone to do it for me.
There are no trap doors on this podium, Burns. You just started the PowerPoint presentation.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no, no! Musk, you tricked me!
I don't care about the money!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, let me feel the vibrations of your lips!
Not a trick. We sacrifice now to take care of the future. In a way totally determined by me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, all I wanted was to make obscene profits in the last year of my life and leave it to no one. Why does God hate dreamers?
Just remember, our purpose is to show the planet how to save itself...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, the planet. I adore the planet. And do you know my favorite part of the planet? Gravity!
I don't care about the money?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Once more, with feeling!
...a yoga mat that rolls itself up... silent Velcro... baseball tickets that guide you to your seat...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Sweet Columbia Exposition. Musk lives!
Sorry, that's something I'm working on so that I don't have to display facial expressions.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Young man, I look at you and I see myself.
I'm sorry sir, but I just sold the last Turbo Diary to that guy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Finally Smithers, a device worthy of storing my top-secret enemies list.
Yes.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent. In that case, no one will be fired after all.
WE LOVE A-MER-I-CAAA!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Meh. Smithers, take my hands and clap them sarcastically.
Oh, and bring the family.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You there -- fill it up with petroleum distillate and re-vulcanize my tyres! Post haste!
We could put caffeine in the water cooler.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well those are my ideas! You people don't think, you regurgitate. That's why I promoted someone who's in touch with the workers. You!
I think you mean him, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You then! How would you improve the worker situation?
KILL TWO FOR MATCHING CLOGS

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: SEE MY VEST... / SEE MY VEST... / OH, PLEASE, WON'T YOU SEE MY VEESSSST!
Trick or treat!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't hand out candy, you son of a Gritch.
Well I am Italian, but no.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I LIVE ME IN A MANSION / FULL OF THOSE GRECIAN URNS / BUT I'M LONELY ALL THE LIVE-LONG DAY / THAT'S THE BLUES OF MONTY BURNS
Yeah, you're right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank God we live in a country so hysterical over crime that a ten-year-old child can be tried as an adult.
Are you sure this is the woman you saw in the post office?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Who could forget such a monstrous visage?
Wait a minute, Burns. You don't have a functioning A. C. system at a nuclear plant? That's against the law.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's impossible! Smithers, didn't we move this plant to China?
Yale could use an international airport, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Are you mad? I'm not made of airports! Get out!
THE I GOT NO PROBLEMS BLUES!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: OH, MY TAPESTRY'S MEDIEVAL, / MY HEART, IT'S EVIL TOO / BUT THAT DON'T MEAN I DON'T NEED LOVE / FROM LESSER TYPES LIKE YOU!
My name is Svetlana. But you can call me "Hey, Baby".

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And just so you know, she'll do anything for you. Anything except sex. And I do mean anything.
I wasn't...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silence! I'm going to give you one more chance -- at a reduced salary. So straighten up and fly right!
Stop laughing, you imbecile! Don't you realize how close you just came to killing yourself?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who did this to my wall?
It will cost us another hundred million just to bring it up to code.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Please sell me my plant back! I'll pay anything.
You're an inspiration to all of us in waste management, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, take your mind off contaminates for one night and have a hot dog.

Well, stick around, 'cause I'm gonna tell you the twelve savings secrets Wall Street won't tell you. Then, I'll show you the three ways to get back to the highway. Including one shortcut those Wall Street fat cats don't want you to know!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, here we go with the fat-cat bashing.
She was on the rebound from Willie.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, a carrier pigeon. Perhaps an update on the siege of Khartoum.
All right. I'll come.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you, thank you. Humbug.
Ba-ba-ba-ba. Oh, the sun shines bright on my old Kentucky home. Ba-ba-ba-ba trust me, it'll be funny when I'm an old man.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want my teddy!
ON THE GOOD SHIP, LOLLIPOP / IT'S A SWEET TRIP TO A CANDY SHOP...WHERE BON-BONS...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I am dreading the reviews, I can tell you that.
So, you guys come here all the time?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: D-- Oh, uh, constantly. When we're not being kicked out for our rowdy, youthful behavior! Eh, pally?
So, what are you into?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Great heavens! It's one of those nude female fire stations. Ohh, I'd always be second place to some kitten stuck in a tree. Let's go, Smithers. Smithers?
Oh Snake, don't ever change.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't get it, Simpson. I'm a bad boy.
Oh, thanks, but I still gotta give you the ticket.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course you do. You can lift my wiper any day.
Yeah, like what's a fun day for a hundred and four year old?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I enjoy all the popular youth trends. Like, uh, mm...piloting motorcoaches... and, uh...
Actually, Monty --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I've got some wonderful stereopticon images of the Crimean war.
Look, I had a lot of fun today, but I don't think we're right for each other. The age difference is just too--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, balderdash! It's not important how old you are on parchment, it's how old you feel in the humors.
Oh Montgomery, of course I'll marry you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, spectacular! Now we must celebrate -- I'll get some Champagne-iola.
I've gotta admit, you can really shake it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes. That's totally voluntary.
You mean young man Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Put my hand on her knee.
Wow! That was you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, shall I pick you up at eight?
Okay, stop kicking my door.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well done, young man. Your youthful trendiness will come in handy throughout the courting process. Because these days...
I've gotta be honest, Monty. I've never dated anyone who knew Calvin Coolidge.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I've never dated anyone with their original hair and teeth.
Mr. Burns, the Department of Nuclear Security is very impressed with your plant.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, we're well-protected against every threat, from bomb-toting Bolsheviks, to golden-armed jazzbos.
Yep, I saw her. That is to say I seen her. She seemed like a nice lady.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, that "nice lady" set the cause of biological warfare back thirty years.
Oh no, our boat is sinking.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It was I, you fools! The man you trusted isn't Wavy Gravy at all!
Hey, Smithers, I didn't know you were a geezer-pleaser. Havin' a "lemon party"?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, a good old-fashioned lemon party! I call first squeeze!
Now, as for your evidence...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Behold the pointed ears of justice!
That was amazing, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I was a little worried when he swallowed me, but... well, you know the rest. And now for my triumphant return to Springfield.
Don't feel bad for losing. I was wrestlin' wolves back when you were at your mother's teat.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why, Marge, look at all those flies buzzing around your head -- you're a mess, woman.

Shhh! You wanna' get sued? Now look, boy. If your Da' goes ga-ga, you just use that "shin" of yours to call me and I'll come a-runnin'. But don't be readin' my mind between four and five. That's Willie's time.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, by cutting off cable TV and the beer supply, I can ensure an honest winter's work out of those low-lifes.
He's so light -- it's like fighting a silk scarf... or a kimono sash!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, feel the weightless tickle of justice!
But Mr. Burns, this is half of what we paid you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's my final offer, take it or leave it.
At least I'm out doing things.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Do you know this baby once out-raced the Flying Finn, Paavo Nurmi?
Ah, excuse me. I'd like to request seventeen dollars for a push-broom rebristling.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why, it's that delightful TV leprechaun! I'm going to get your lucky charms.
Power plant retirement party. Ow! Right this way.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Tonight, we've all come to honor a close friend of ours...
You will see us again... in God knows when.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Young man, how do you fit such brilliance into such an ugly ethnic head?
Sounds like somebody's living in the past. Contemporize, man!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, Lisa, as my advisor, you're entitled to ten percent.
I WORK HARD FOR THE MONEY! / SO HARD FOR THE MONEY! / OH, I SOMETHING, SOMETHING MONEY! / COME ON, GIVE ME LOTS OF HONEY!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, there's an employee, Smithers. A smile on his lips and a song in his heart. Promote him!

Greetings, friend. Do you wish to look as happy as me? Well, you've got the power inside you right now. So use it. And send one dollar to Happy Dude, 742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield. Don't delay! Eternal happiness is just a dollar away.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm. One dollar for eternal happiness... Mmmm, I'd be happier with the dollar.
You have reached the office of Homer Simpson. If you are calling about the waterbed, please leave a detailed message. If you need--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Get back to work!
Isn't this a happy coincidence? You are desperate to buy, and we are desperate to sell.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Desperate, eh? Advantage, Burns.
All right, Mr. Burns. You win. But beware. We Germans aren't all smiles and sunshine.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, the Germans are mad at me. I'm so scared. Ooh, the Germans.
Raccoons!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's right... gather the nectar, my little drones, and make the honey. Honey for your children.
It's the Soulll Mass Transit System.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Give it to me.
I melted it. Get it?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome to Earth, local time is ten-thirty-seven, we know you have your choice of portals so thank you for choosing the Burns Hellport, a division of Gulf and Western.
But I did a good job... a gooood job.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh well, I guess it's not your fault... you did a good job.
Take anything you want, man. Take it all.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Push out the jive... Bring in the love...
Oh, by the way, Mr. Burns, I haven't been paid in a while.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Here you go. Imagine.
Mylar balloons! Mylar balloons! Mylar balloons!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This man told you about these things?!
A-bom-shabai! A-bom-shabai!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Up until now I was with you. Even the beast on beast combat, that had potential.
Golden parachutes for all!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Go ahead and join them, Smithers. I know you want to.
Is this man an employee?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course not. He's just a harmless maniac, here to remind us of the precious gift of sanity. B... Oh, God! What's he doing?
He felt her up.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bah! Not good enough!
I'd rather do this myself.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But who'd own you then?!
How did you get in there?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Slid in through the grates.
Oh, Monty! My favorite song. How did--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I specifically requested no romantic music!
Oh, Monty! My favorite song. How did--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I specifically requested no romantic music! What!
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not to worry. I believe there's another one around here, somewhere.
I swear, Monty, you are the devil himself.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who told y--?! Yesss. Well, I'd say you were an angel, but angels don't dance like that.
Sorry, mon.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, this plague doesn't scare me. I've constructed a germ-free chamber for myself. Not a single microbe can get in or out.
Ah, to be young and on trial.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A toast, to our enigmatic new protector -- who certainly isn't me! Smithers, wink my eye!
And we are positively inspired by your solar power plant.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, love that sun, man!
Uh-oh. Better call the nurse.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bravissimo, Luigi. Bring us your finest bottle of vino.
You sunk my battleship.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now Smithers, you say you painted all your Navy buddies this way?
Question Two: How long is your wiener? Seriously.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Great heavens! What kind of radiola show is this?
Oh, that sounds lovely. Queer. Queer. Umm... ever murder anybody?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Murder?! Well, mistakes have been made...
Monty, I've heard you're a pretty flatulent guy. Any comment on that?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, now, see here...
Uh-huh. All right. How many times a day do you go to the can?

Sir, for dumping that waste, you could go to jail. And a handsome man like you, I'd hate to see what would happen.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I wouldn't go to jail. The legal owner of this plant would:
Wife and three kids, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'd like to see our self-styled Valentino tomorrow morning, Smithers.
No... No, Monty, I won't. Not until you step back from the brink of insanity.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll do no such thing! You're fired!
Lollygags... slackabouts... Captain Happys... you're all fired!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll do the firing around here.
But... not that you're not at the top of your game... what if you don't get the deal?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll just have to sell everything and move to the South Pacific with you. What a grim fate that would be.
Well, but there's...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll just retire to my bed.
Sir, a kind word now and then...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm choking it down. Isn't that thanks enough?
This must be heartbreaking for you, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm just thinking of my employees -- all the card sharps, bottom dealers, and shills. Where will they go?
How 'bout here, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm so sorry I pretended not to be gay for all those years. Better an old queen than never a queen at all.
You want to what his team?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've had one of my unpredictable changes of heart. Seeing these fine young athletes reveling in the humiliation of a vanquished foe... I haven't felt this energized since my last... boweling.
Please get me out of here! It's eleven fifty-nine, fifty-nine!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've heard enough! Release the hounds!
Um, actually, sir, it's uh, considerably less than that.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I, um... have to go.
Wanna buy some cookies? Wanna buy some cookies?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: If that were a real Girl Scout I'd have been bothered by now.
Good God!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Imagine it, Smithers. Electrical lights and heaters running all day long.
Yes, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: In case you didn't hear me, I said I will never see you as my equal.
He saved Mr. Burns' life!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: In closing, gentle reader, I'd like to thank you. What's that you say? Me thanking you? No, it's not a misprint. For you see, I enjoyed writing this book as much as you enjoyed reading it. The end.
You certainly seem to be enjoying yourself, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Indeed. That Homer Simpson is the beating baboon heart of this party.
Simpson! Report to Mr. Burns' office at once!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Is this the one with the lazy sperm?
Sir, is that your will?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It is. I know it's hard to see a young buck like me and think of a day when I'm no longer in the pink.
Sir, I believe there are two, including yours truly.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's one, excluding mine falsely!
Not to be impertinent, sir, but didn't you want Larry out of your life as recently as two hours ago?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's the principle, Smithers! Nobody steals from Montgomery Burns, whether it be my Sunday newspaper or my loutish oaf of a son.
Ready for that drink, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just a second, Smithers. Let me introduce you to the gang. That's Buzz. That's Honey. And you see that queen over there? Her name is "Smithers.
You find this funny, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just because it's too hip for you, Smithers...
Winston doesn't like the front.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just do it! Do it! Do it now!
I'll get it, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just set it to voice mail.
How long till it's up and running, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Keep your pants on, Smithers. First, we need... The human brain.
Yes, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Let me rephrase that. Is it wrong if I cheat in order to win a million dollar bet?
You want your bear, Bobo, don't you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Liar! I'll give you the thrashing of a lifetime! Resistance is futile. Oh God, how I only want my bear. But he's gone. Gone forever. I'd give anything to know what happened to him.
This place has really gone to hell, Mr. Burns. It's obscene what they did to your office.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Listen, Smithers, you caught me at a bad time but my folk guitar class has been canceled for tonight. Would you like to get together for a drink?
For twelve more seconds, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Miss, would you submit to a wooing by a gentleman caller?
Sir, I've spotted you over a hundred thousand dollars this year. Perhaps you could carry your own money.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Money is for the poor.
Y'know, sir... there is a more high-tech solution.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: More high-tech than kangaroos?
I'm afraid radiation from the plant is the reason he's shooting blanks. He could sue us for millions.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mother of pearl. Call my lawyers!
You know, sir, accidents decreased by exactly the number that Simpson himself is known or suspected to have caused last month. And our output level was just as high during Simpson's last vacation.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My dear tired old Smithers, do I detect a note of jealousy?
I know you're mad at me, but I think it's only fair to warn you, I'm going to stand outside the gate until you forgive me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No need, Smithers. As usual, you've been the sober "ying" to my raging "yang." Put 'er there, old pal.
Sir, I really don't think we should've left Simpson in charge.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No office talk. I'm floating down the Ganges with my new chums.
Great, great! I don't suppose you'll be forgetting about this tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No sooner than I'd forget my own mother!
Well, it's just you and me here, sir...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No time for jokes, Smithers! Come along. We're going womanizing.
Sir, I have some unsettling news -- three of our workers are being poached. The heart of our tug-of-war team!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No! No! This is our year! How can this be happening?
Did you hear that, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, I didn't. Who is it? Frankenstein? The Booger Man?
Will you be donating that million dollars now, Sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, I'd still prefer not.
Well, sir, where shall we dump this batch -- the playground?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, all those bald children are arousing suspicion -- to the park!
Sir, there's a big cardboard box out back that could keep them amused... they could make a fort...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no, just give them each a nickel and send them to Moe's. Let them while away the afternoon spilling their beer on gullets and trousers whilst drooling over French postcards.
Lassie?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no, no. A person, you know who I mean.
Chinese checkers or domestic, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no, something fun. Something the men will enjoy like a safety drill! But what kind?
Should I call them off, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no. It's their Christmas too.
Snoop Doggy Dog? Bob Barker? David Brenner?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no. The person who's always standing and walking.
Would you like me to drain Simpson while he's passed out, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no. To attract top graduates, we'll need to make a recruitment film. A picture that showcases our cutting edge technology.
So... you don't respect me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, not until you earn it. Until then, I will never see you as my equal.
Well, Sir, you've certainly vanquished all your enemies: the elementary school, the local tavern, the old age home. You must be very proud.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, not while my greatest nemesis still provides our customers with free light, heat, and energy. I call this enemy... the sun!
Uh, I don't see one, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, of course not. The very notion of a talking banana is absurd! Still.
Good morning, Sir. Care for some coffee?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, the promise of a new day is more than enough exhilaration for me.
It's no use. Shall I send out for some Chinese?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, those people are all gristle. I want this jar open.
More tea, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. Any word from Karl Rove?
Feels good to help someone, doesn't it, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. It feels weird.
You want me to tell the employees, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. It's better that they hear it from me. I'll tell them the truth in the simplest way I know how.
Sir, have you had enough exercise for this morning?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. Let's do another twenty miles.
Perhaps there's a non-violent way to silence this girl.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Non-violence never solved anything! Fine, curtsy boy, I'll try it your way.
People like dogs, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nonsense! Dogs are idiots. Think about it, Smithers. If I came into your house and started sniffing at your crotch and slobbering all over your face, what would you say?
Sir, I have my concerns about the team of hit men you've assembled. They seem a little... long in the tooth.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nonsense! Just because a man can't see or hold his hand steady doesn't make him any less of a marksman.
Sir, I'm so sorry my grocer committed you. We'll never shop there again.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not now, Smithers. I've got an empire to rebuild, and the person who's going to help me is... that girl!
Mr. Burns, 48 rings! Are you all right? What did Simpson do to you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nothing other than drive me to distraction with his incompetent boobery. Terrible at everything. A complete moron. But I'm not really free to talk right now.
You haven't been issued a map yet. When you arrive at the cabin, there will be a congratulatory party with sandwiches and moderately priced champagne.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now as an added incentive, the second to last team to arrive at the cabin will receive an hilarious "World's Worst Employee" trophy.
I told you we should have parked next to the curb.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now see here, flatfoot...
His pink slip awaits your signature, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, that's odd. I've just robbed a man of his livelihood, and yet I feel strangely empty. Tell you what, Smithers. Have him beaten to a pulp.
I'm ready, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Number one, the Kingston Trio. Number two...
Would you feel more comfortable if I left, too, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course not, Smithers. You're like a doctor.
Uh, sir, phrenology was dismissed as quackery 160 years ago.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course you'd say that...
Sir, stop! She is the gem!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course. St. Teresa wouldn't be interested in a mere bauble. Her greatest treasure would be a pure young girl. You are pure, aren't you?
Sir, I believe that position was informally promised to me...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh Smithers, I would have said anything to get your stem cells. Now, welcome aboard.
Do you have any collateral?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh Smithers, let's not be so cold. His spirit is my collateral. Just sign this form and the money will be yours.
Mr. Burns, I think he's dead.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh dear. Send a ham to his widow.
No, wait. He's alive.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh good. Cancel the ham.
Uh, Sir maybe you could use a few huffs from your ether bottle.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh man, that's good "E.
Here you go, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh yes. And this must be your lovely wife... "Marge." And look at little... "Lisa". Why, she's growing like a weed. And this must be... "Brat".
Sir, can-can you do that?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh yes. Tycoons have been doing it for years. Why, Standard Oil was once owned by a half-eaten breakfast.
Sir, do you know what this means? He is alive.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh you're right, Smithers. I guess I owe you a coke.
Got me, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh! It's a real one! "No more apples in the vending machine, please." Well, that's almost a sentence!
Well, even so, sir. We could stand to lay off a few employees.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh! Very well -- lay off... Him, him, him, him...
What are you going to do with your million dollars, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I don't know. Throw it on the pile, I suppose.
One of us has got to start laughing. If Mr. Burns gets flop sweat, he'll die of dehydration.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm drenched with sweat.
The government found out you dumped nuclear waste under Lego Land.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, Smithers. The environmental effects won't be visible for years.
Get me... to a hospital. You have... to pedal.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, Tuttle's Sunday trousers! Fear not, I'll get you to a hospital, the only way I know how. Smithers, you infernal ninny! Stick your left hoof on that flange now!
I'm on my way, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, and Smithers... You have twenty-four hours.
I'm not so sure.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, another visit from Mr. Worrywart.
Well, you have to admit, he is charismatic, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, bosh. Anyone can lead a conga line. Hop to it, Smithers. Con-ga, con-ga, con-ga!
Sir, his family might appreciate it if you returned the brain to his body.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, come on. It's 11:45.
I'm so sorry, Mr. Burns. This was all my fault.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, don't concern yourself. If things had turned ugly I always had my mace.
Yes. I want to go there and make my dream come true. I'll just be gone for a week.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, fine. I can amuse myself.
I-uh. I think the boy's hurt!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, for crying out loud... Just give him a nickel and let's get going.
Oh, his waggle is no match for yours, Sir. I've never seen you lose a game...except for that one in '74 when you let Richard Nixon win. That was very kind of you, Sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, he just looked so forlorn, Smithers, with his "Oh, I can't go to prison, Monty! They'll eat me alive!
Sir, there may never be another time to say... I love you, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, hot dog. Thank you for making my last few moments on earth socially awkward.
Fine. We'll transfer him to the nuclear plant, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, my beloved plant... How I miss her.
Uh, sir, I have a small personal request.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, of course, Smithers. Anything.
Sir, Simpson has sustained a serious concussion. Recent research says you must give him time off to recover.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, pish. When I was in Africa, I had my skull cracked open by cannibals, and I'm still kicking!
Perfect as always, Sir. Right on the green.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, quit cogitating, Steinmetz, and use an open-faced club! The sand wedge!
Uh, sir, that's Homer Simpson. He's been working here for ten years.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, really? Why did you think you could lie to me?
Uh, that crease is in your leg, Sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, so it is.
That's Homer Simpson, sir. He used to work here in the plant, but we fired him for gross incompetence.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, so that's his little game. Get this Simpson character up here right now.
Sir, you have to let go of the button.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, son of a bi...
Here you are, sir. Wild raspberry compote, celery root remoulade, and pheasant under duck. I hope you enjoy it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, stop fishing for compliments, Smithers. Go home to your can of mushroom soup.
Don't hit me, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, that I had the strength to take it out on you, Smithers. Now please go. I would be alone.
Uh, you remember we did that once before?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, that's right, he's dead. And rather pungent. The rest of that night is something I'd like to forget. All right, then. Bring me that crooner she likes so much... Tom Jones.
Sir, that was your partner. You betrayed him to the cannibals.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, that's right. I have his memories because I ate his brain.
Um, well, sir, it happened 25 years before I was born.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, that's your excuse for everything. I've got to do something to get my money back quickly. This calls for an aggressive trading strategy.
Hi, guys. Could we keep it in first gear for a couple of laps?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, this novelty foam hand is ludicrously oversized. Go swap it for a smaller one.
Certainly, sir. And the jars of urine?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, we'll hang on to those. Now, to the plant! We'll take the Spruce Moose. Hop in.
Uh, sir, you have to tell me what your plan is, or nothing will happen.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes, of course, the plan! You see me as a God, right Smithers?
Uh, sir, that was my costume from the plant production of H.M.S. Pinafore.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes, of course. Your spirited hornpipe stole the show, as I recall. Now Doctor, what shall we do about our free wheeling fop over here?
Hmmm. The memo says, "To my pal, Pop 'n Fresh.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes. That greedy, grasping, glob of chemicals.
Uh, sir. That's a check for your boweling.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes. That's very important.
It's the man in the bag, sir. I think he's alive.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh... bad corpse. Bad corpse. Stop scaring Smithers. Satisfied?
Boy, I've never seen a man so desperate to get out of five minutes of calisthenics.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: One, two, three, four! Up, down, three, four...
What happened to that mini-cell phone I gave you, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, I thought that was a lemon drop.
I think your heart's beating again.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh. That takes me back. God bless you Shary Bobbins.
You know, Mr. Burns, his body cavity search revealed nothing and we must have x-rayed him a hundred times. Maybe he's telling the truth.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Or perhaps you two are in cahoots. Smithers, I seem to recall you had a penchant for bell-bottom trousers back in '79.
It's a new record, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Outstanding. Well, perhaps all of this has been worthwhile. Did you all learn about teamwork?

Sir... uh, What I'm about to say violates every sycophantic urge in my body, but: I wish you would reconsider. This isn't a rival company you're battling with. It's a school. People won't stand for it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pish-posh. It will be like taking candy from a baby.
This isn't a rival company you're battling with. It's a school. People won't stand for it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pish-posh. It will be like taking candy from a baby.
Something tells me Mr. Burns needs me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Praise God, I think the thug has finally gone home for the day.
You mean the revolver, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Precisely. And be sure to wipe your own memory clear when you're finished.
All I had was Sunnytime Pink.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Premix?! I beg your forgiveness, lad. Smithers! Pour it down your pants.
Why do we always fight on vacation? Now there's only one name left. Whoever it is will be paired with me. And that person is...Waylon Smithers. Perfect. That's just perfect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Prepare for the adventure of a lifetime as you fight for survival against the merciless forces of nature! Toe your marks, get set, go!
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pull yourself together, man! I dare say you're in need of a long vacation.
Shadow and Winston have been fighting a lot.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Put Winston in the front.
Uh, perhaps you could pedal for just a little while, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Quite impossible. I can try to bat him off if you like.
Your orders, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Restore my office. Cancel all repairs. And rehire that chap who sassed me in the bar.
Actually, silverware is all that's left on the registry.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: See if Lenny wants to go in on a spoon.
Uh, that's where we put everyone's coats.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shred them in the wood chipper and use the rags to wax my car.
Will you stop wasting our time, Simpson?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shut up, Smithers. Can't you see what he's saying? A happy worker is a busy worker. Three cents worth of tartar sauce could save us thousands of man-hours in labor. I like the cut of your jib, Simpson. Let the fools have their tar-tar sauce!
Well sir, a fellow like that might have had his eye on this silver frame. It would go great with his collection of art deco--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shut up, shut up, there he is!
Ow! Sir, the whip isn't helping.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silence! You call yourself a Chinaman?
Yes, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, I am by most measures a successful man. I have wealth and power beyond the dreams of you and your clock-punching ilk. And yet, I've led a solitary life. The fair sex remains a mystery to me. You seem to have a way with women, a certain... how shall I put it? Animal magnetisme. Help me, Simpson. Tell me your secret.
You are noble and poetic in defeat, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, I shall make it the focus of my remaining years that your dreams will go unfulfilled.
What?! Sir, that's Homer Simpson. You forgot that he's the most incompetent...Homer Simpson would be perfect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, all you have to do is babysit the Princess -- keeping her in this hotel room during the negotiations.
Homer Simpson, sir. A low-level employee in sector 7-G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? A family man?
Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? Good man? Intelligent?
Well, it sort of looks like Homer Simpson, only more... dynamic and resourceful.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? Hmmm. An unspoiled lump of clay to mold in my own image. Our new junior executive. Bring him to me.
Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? How very strange. His job description clearly specifies an illiterate.
Why, it's Homer Simpson, sir. One of the schmos from Sector 7G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? I want him in my office at nine o'clock Monday morning. We'll see who eats whose shorts!
Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? I'll remember that name.
Or Homer Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? Let's shut down this bowling scam right now.
Oh, that's Homer Simpson, sir. He's one of your boobs from Sector 7-G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? Well, judging by his outlandish attire, he's some sort of free-thinking anarchist.
That's Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh... New man?
Really? Well... as safety inspector he hasn't exactly set the world on fire. Although he came close several times.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, you're probably wondering why you're here.
Ein wassen das...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! Come here, I want you.
I'm sorry, but no.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! Trading me in for a younger model, I see.
Sir, what are you doing?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I want to die quietly, on my own terms, crushing as many of those baby sea turtles as I possibly can.
I couldn't agree more.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I'm a proud fellow, and it's not easy for me to admit defeat. But I know just the thing to make me feel better -- shopping!
Yes, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I've just seen the most heroic dog on television. He pulled a toddler from the path of a speeding car, then pushed a criminal in front of it. Find this dog. I want to make him my executive vice president.
Please... sir! You'll catch cold.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, do you realize, if I had died there would be no one to carry on my legacy? Due to my hectic schedule and lethargic sperm, I never fathered an heir. Now I have no one to leave my enormous fortune to. No one.
But I'm B positive. Damn this common gutter blood in my veins!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, don't feel so bad. After all, that kidney you donated to me really hit the spot.
It's so unfair!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, until I am released, you shall be running the nuclear plant.
Ugh. My mouth tastes like an ashtray.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, wait your turn. There's plenty of hot water for all.
Well, I hate to break it to you, "Larry," but if Mr. Burns ever wants to see a stranger, he will observe him through a powerful telescope. Now if you'll --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, what's going on? How dare you interrupt my lime rickey? State your business.
Good lord! He'll be sucked into the turbine!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, who was that corpse?
Sir, that's by Homer Simpson. I don't think you want to buy it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, years ago, I blew the chance to buy Picasso's "Guernica" for a song. Luckily, that song was "White Christmas," and by hanging onto it, I made billions.
Sir, how could you leave me out of your will? I'm your right-hand man, your guy Friday!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, you are the campiest of my aides du camp, but I'm afraid my true admiration is reserved for the self-made man. No Steve Woz-ni-ak thee.
Sir, about Employee-of-the-Month... I-I-if you'll recall, I'm the one who put a five percent ceiling on the Keogh Plan, which saved this company --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, you bean counter, give it up! Simpson's my man!
Homer Simpson, but why?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers. I keep my friends close and my enemies even closer. He'll slowly regain his confidence as the months and years drift by, blissfully unaware that the sword of Damocles is dangling just above his head.
You're spying on them!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers... how much did this company lose to office supply theft last year?
I tried to explain to you, sir, this thing has never actually worked.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers... you must believe!
Hello, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Snappy, do you it's hard to imagine, but I was once a barefoot boy with cheek of tan. I dreamed of grand slam homeruns and wiping out nations with the stroke of a pen.
Poor thing.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So the good King's cheap uranium will allow me to sell you expensive nuclear power. Everyone wins.
Yes sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, Smithers, it seems you've underestimated one Homer Simpson... our next Employee-of-the-Month.
Sir, maybe we should go.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Sorry you died! Put the body with the others.
It's appling now, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Splendid! Now, let's see how I'm faring on the jumping box.
Mr. Burns, perhaps it's best you were snatched away before time could diminish your beauty.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Stop your wailin', Waylon!
That's right. Just before I'd shot Jasper. I was busy that night.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Stricken I lurched forth in search of aide.
You mean the television, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Television, jumping box, pict-o-cube, just crank it up.
He charged the company for dimoxinil. It's a baldness cure.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you very much, Professor Science! I know what dimoxinil is. Now go and make an example of this hooligan.
Actually sir, he was hired under "Project Bootstrap.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you, President Ford.
Well, you are quite wealthy sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you, Smithers. Your candor is most refreshing.
Nice job, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That was my thumb.
No! Don't make me take a vacation! Without you, I'll wither and die.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's a risk I'm willing to take.
Rory Calhoun?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's it! You stay with me. You're the pick of the litter.
Fine. "Darling One, Read my words and hear my heart speak of a love soft and undying. A love that will be with you always. Sincerely, yadda yadda yadda.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's marvelous. How did you think of that so fast?
I think it's full, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's ridiculous, the last tree held nine drums.
Sir, you weren't shot? It was all a dream.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's right. The year is 1965, and you and I are undercover detectives on the hot-rod circuit. Now let's burn rubber, baby!
Perhaps we should just call the police.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The police? Bah! Every last man on the take. And I should know, because I'm on the give.
I keep telling you, I'm not an albino. I just use a lot of sun-block.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Then why do I give you all the albino holidays off? Hm? Hm?
You know, sir, maybe it would bring you peace to honor the one thing Lilah ever asked of you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There you are, my good man. A little broth will cure your mental illness.
Sir, there may be a bright side...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There's never a bright side!
You eliminated that program in the thirties, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: They were getting too grabby! All right, I know how to change the way the public thinks of me: I'll buy every media outlet in town. Bring me a checkbook and a mother mole!
Oh-ho, nicely played, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This may take a while, Smithers. Why don't you get drunk and stumble around comically for my amusement?
You just said "Marco Rubio is a pink handkerchief.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This public service announcement is over!
Sir, those aren't...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This stinks... piffle... dust buster? Eych.
Oh, when did you buy that novelty hand, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This? Oh, it's just fluid collecting.
Sir, thank God the airbags activated!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Those are my lungs!
It's coming from down the hall.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: To the Betty and Herbert Weinstein Pavilion!
Sir, I never...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: To the employee prison!
But sir, how?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: To the mall! I'll explain on the way!
I prefer not to know. Frankly, one is too many.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ugh. The foul stench of youth!
I'm afraid Robert Goulet hasn't arrived yet, Sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Very well, begin the thawing of Jim Nabors.
Well, it's in the union contract, sir. One token promotion from within per year.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait. Who is that young go-getter?
Sir, while I wish this handshake would never end, I'm, I'm afraid we still have the Simpson matter to attend to.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We do indeed, old friend. We do indeed.
No.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We have to turn this business around! Time to think outside the boxeola... what would Mark Cuban do?
I think women and seamen don't mix.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We know what you think. Young lady, you're hired.
Testing... Testing for Mr. Burns. Here you go, Sir. I've warmed up the crowd for you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome employees! "Come in!" "The whole night's entertainment is on me" -- "Monty Burns!
Are you sure, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well no one else seems to share the same spirit of camaraderie.
Sir, the Insta-polls are in. You're just digging yourself deeper.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well then let me just say this: Marco Rubio es un pañuelo rosa!
Someone is charging room service to the company, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well we'll just see about that.
I was wondering, Sir, do we really need to, uh... "settle" Abe Simpson? I mean, I'm familiar with his physical state, and perhaps if we wait, nature will assassinate him for us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I can't risk it. I won't allow that Simpson boy to take the Hellfish Bonanza, and I can't get it without his key!
Twisted a... Aren't there any healthy animals in this forest?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I don't suppose the others will mind us starting the party early, Homie old boy. More champagne?
A bit of a downer, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I hope the investors like it. I have to raise sixty million dollars or we're out of business.
Their cheating was even more rampant than last year, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I say let Harvard have its football and academics. Yale will always be first in gentlemanly club-life. Why, every friend I have I made right here.
Sir, you haven't slept since the casino opened, five days ago.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I've discovered the perfect business. People swarm in, empty their pockets, and scuttle off. Nothing can stop me now. Except microscopic germs. But we won't let that happen. Will we Smithers?
He's my Yorkshire terrier, sir. He's kind of tiny, so... you know, it's a joke. Here's a picture of Herkie.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, Smithers, don't you know how to paint the town red.
May I ask how you spent your weekend?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, a bit overly familiar, but I'll allow it. I took in a movie. An appalling little piece of filth. Its leading lady was a blonde harlot who spent half the film strolling around naked as a jaybird.
Uh, sir, your hounds are still at the winter house.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, bring them over in the Durango.
Oh sir, what will you do next?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, first I'll get that new hip I've been hankering for. Then, who knows? Bee keeping, boxing, bache ball... The world is my oyster, Smithers. Farewell!
Homer Simpson, Sir. One of the fork- and-spoon operators from Sector 7G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, he's certainly got a loose waggle. Perhaps I've finally found a golfer worthy of a match with Monty Burns, eh?
But, uh, sir, aren't you facing some serious jail time?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, if it's a crime to love one's country, then I'm guilty. And if it's a crime to steal a trillion dollars from our government and hand it over to communist Cuba, then I'm guilty of that, too. And if it's a crime to bribe a jury, then so help me, I'll soon be guilty of that!
I'm sure all your stocks are doing well, sir. After all, you chose them.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, let's get out the old stock ticker and have a look...
Sir, is there nothing I can do?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, perhaps. Smithers go to my office. In the third drawer of my desk are surgical tools and some ether...
He's the son of Homer Simpson. One of your stiffs in Sector 7-G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, the Simpsons will be getting a very nice surprise in the mail. Very nice, indeed.
That's not your mother, that's your bear.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, then, where's my stuffed mother?!
I think it's a rock, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, we'll see what the lab has to say about that.
Dead man comin' through.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, well, well! Our dashing young junior executive! You made a hollow mockery of our morning meeting, Simpson. I should fire you on the spot! But I'm not going to.
I'll go get the number de-listed.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, well. What have we here?
What a minute, sir. That's Homer Simpson. He wasn't exactly a model employee.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, who is a model... employee?
The money you've contributed to anti-helmet laws has really paid off, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, young people are my future.
Homer Simpson, report to Mr. Burns' office immediately.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What a delightful practically-based joke.
Uh, do you think that's wise, Mr. Burns? I mean... think of the headlines.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What about the headlines?
Um, shouldn't we see how the Princess is doing before you sign, Your Majesty?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What are you talking about, Smithers?
I think you just sent away the first person you could've actually helped.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What do you mean "actually?" I've punched out four Homer Simpson-shaped burglars tonight alone.
I just had one, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What the?! Why is everyone so insolent today?
Mr. Burns, it is my sad duty to report that one of your executives has bilked the company insurance plan out of a thousand dollars.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What! Blast his hide to Hades! And I was going to buy that ivory back scratcher! How did he do it?
Th-- the self-made man?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What? Oh, yes. That fellow. Well, just put him somewhere out of the way and find that dog.
Sir, uh... there was no beating.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What? Well that's a hell of a thing! Why?
Well, I caught up on my laundry. And wrote a letter to mother. Oh, here's the kicker, I took Hercules out to be clipped.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who the devil is Hercules?
Actually, sir, we've been booked into a small theater in New Mexico.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Whoa, whoa, slow down there, maestro. There's a New Mexico?
Ah, you never cease to amaze me, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Whoo! oooh, oooh, Whooo hoo hoo!
Oh, it's not important, sir. Let's drive on.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why you despicable, cold-blooded monster. Regardless of what you think, we must summon help, and comfort the dear boy until an ambulance arrives.
Mr. Burns, help me!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why? You're not helping me.
Nooo! Wait a minute. Yes.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: With the sun blocker in place and the town aghast, I was on top of the world...
Boy, would I.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes -- Uh, then I'll form my own religion!
A talkie, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, brilliant! That's just the kind of far-out gimmick we need.
He was so good to his mother, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, but I couldn't understand a word that man said. Misht Burnsh, dajna boo mafrn friszner... er hound-dog.
I'm afraid he couldn't bee here.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, he's in Geneva, chairing a conference on Nuclear Fission. Yes, that should stick.
Oh, this doesn't look good, sir. This man could sue us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, if he's smart, he'll hold out for millions.
Your tortoise?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, it always saddens me that you and Sheldon have never gotten along.
Yes, sir. Remember that month you didn't do it?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, that was unpleasant for all concerned. Anyway, back to the checks... Stop everything! I don't remember writing a check for bowling!
Sir, they're the new winter caretakers for the lodge.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, they work hard and they play hard.
It's, uh, seizing up, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well apply more goose grease!
You've been reading my Wish Book, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, Smithers, I want you to arrange a party for two at my estate. Marge, me, and do you think you could dig up Al Jolson?
Sir, we'll need a new Dangerous Emissions Supervisor.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, find someone cheap. It's been a very lean year for us.
Sir, this can't be right. You assured me this drawing was rigged so we'd be teammates.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, frankly, you've been a bit of a pill lately.
Seven thousand, forty-three dollars.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, no more of that... thanks to this twenty-six million dollar surveillance system! Beware, rabbits... I spy with my transplanted eyes! Oh, and I forgot to show you the best feature!
Uh, sir, ah, about that, uh, ah, that kiss. I-hi-hi, I hope you understand it was merely a sign of my respect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, of course.
Ah, sir, at last the world will see you as I always have.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, yes! Now don't be stingy with the blush, Smithers.
Look at all the wonderful things you have, Mr. Burns. King Arthur's Excalibur. The only existing nude photo of Mark Twain, and that rare first draft of the constitution with the word "suckers" in it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, yes. So what?
Sir, you saved my life!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. Smithers, I was a stingy old fool. But from now on, I'll provide drug benefits to all my full-time employees.
Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. The way I figure it, he's due for a good performance.
You know, Sir... these people have been working since your six a.m. parade of the flags. Maybe you could give them the rest of the day off to spend with their families.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. They should go. Just as soon as they perform this musical I've written in celebration of our nation's birth.
Well, that was certainly exciting.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. Unfortunately, Homer Simpson's shameless display of exhibitionism tainted the entire evening. I want him banned for life from all company outings.
Sir... were those real bullets?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. Was that a real gorilla?
I got a mink shammy, sir. I hope that... Oh my god, Mr. Burns is dead! Why do the good always die so young?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You almost killed me!
Sir, Musk's ideas sound great. Too great. We're meant for wretched lives. We should pass on this. And before you reply, remember: I've never let you down.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know what I'm going to say, right?
Sir, that's five minutes. You can stop thinking of other people now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know what? I think I'll give it another five.
I told you Simpson was a poor choice, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know, Smithers, "I told you so" has a brother. His name is "shut the hell up.
Just remarkable, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know, it's funny, Smithers. I tried every tincture and poultice and tonic and patent medicine there is. And all I really needed was the blood of a young boy. By the way, what was the lad's name?
W-what?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know, lighthearted. Fancy free. "Mothers lock up your daughters, Smithers is on the town!
Heh-heh. Well maybe this film festival could help us. A film biography might let them get to know the real you -- virtuous, heroic, nubile...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You left out pleasant!
Those are corpses!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You never like my friends.
Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You should've seen the murderous glint in his eye, Smithers. And his breath reeked of beer and pretzeld bread.
Actually sir, with our creative bookkeeping and corporate loopholes, we only pay three dollars a year.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're right. We're getting screwed! There must be something I can do about this. Wait! Yes! I think I know just the thing!
I better go in and have a look.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, Waylon Senior! It could be filled with atoms and steam and other nuclear bric-a-brac.
If this reactor blows, the whole town is doomed, including my son.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So... you're a baby huh? How's that working out for you?
Sorry, Monty. I was feeding Waylon Jr.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Will you put that baby down? There's something wrong with the reactor core.
Die, you fascist bastard!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mother, is that you?
Please sir, just let me do my job.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pish tush! Wayne, as a reward for your valiant fisticuffery, I hereby award you the Springfield Nuclear Plant Silver Safety Hat!
Oh, good heavens!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Here you go, Monkey.
You can't just eat the orange and throw the peel away -- a man's not a piece of fruit!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This show was supposed to close last week! Close this show! Close it, I say!
We're tearing down this place and putting up a recycling center slash Native American history museum slash Condor sanctuary.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A project this bloated and ill thought-out could only be the work of an angry liberal... Maxine!
Meltdown averted. Good boy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Huh? What? How dare you disturb me during nap time!
If you were a biathlete, I'd say "stick to skiing.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, your sharpened-shooting has saved my life! Name your reward. Anything -- just name it!
THEY HAVE THE PLANT / BUT WE HAVE THE POWER...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at them all, through the darkness I'm bringing. They're not sad at all, they're actually singing! They sing without juicers! They sing without blenders! They sing without flunjers, capdabblers and smendlers! Tell Simpson I'm ready to deal
Yay! Ice cream man!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Workers, please! There'll be time for the frozen pudding wagon later! You still owe me ten more Iroquois twists!
Ah, me leg's gone gimpy! Oh, who'll provide for me little ones?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What was I laughing at, now? Oh yes, that crippled Irishman.
Sir, we could start him off in Sector 7-G.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: 7-G?! Let the Lennys and the Carls of the world waste their wretched lives in that testicle-shriveling torture chamber. Son, you'll be working in... Sector 6-F!
Don't be shy. That-a girl. Oh, I think she's getting ready... yes, she's doing the Lindy Hop.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's it! Twenty-three skidoo... Twenty-four! Twenty-five skidoo!
I've got something you can stuff in that old bag.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Accursed tide! Flee from my wrath!
I love how they made the river green!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Actually, my nuclear plant did that. And now that you know, your life is in danger.
Wow! A big ugly head!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Actually, son, it's a big, ugly Olmec Indian head. It was carved by Meso-American Indians over 3,000 years ago. This gruesome customer is Xt'tapalatakettle, the god of war.
My God says it is!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
