dialogue.text: Ah, I see you're ice cold with anticipation.
We'll tell ya, mom.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, tie game. Bottom of the ninth, two outs, bases loaded, Strawberry coming up...
Who cares?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And what's that alarming sound? Smithers, get in here! Smithers!
But...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And worst of all, you took the "Hamburglar's" birthday off last Monday and Wednesday! Which is it? Now, my voice is giving out, so I'm just going to poke you for the next hour or so.
Gotcha. Can't win, don't try.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: As your new manager, I want to say this up front. No one is assured a spot in the starting line-up. I don't care if your name is Steve Sax, Darryl Strawberry, or... Smithers, what's one of the bad players' names?
Um, uh, I think I'd like to go home.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Aw, if you stay you can have anything you want to eat, even some sort of gelatin dish. It's made from hooves, you know.
You were once the youngest of something?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But fortune ended up smiling on me while snuffing the life from my siblings.
Sorry. You've gotta admit it's catchy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Come on, Smithers. Let's go finish the little flea circuses off. Except for "Little Monty," of course.
Now she just bottles up her misery like a normal mom!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Gentlemen, my prison is losing money. We need more convicts in the dungeonareum.
I'm picking respect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good to see you. Glad you could make it.
Shouldn't we wait for the other babies before we open the presents?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Guess what happened to me last night!
Whoa! He's here!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello, Homer. Marge, you look dazzling. Oh, and look, I've brought noodle kugel.
Hey Cryptkeeper, I like your Dodge Scare-a-van.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How dare you mock my mobile-a-mobile? It was the first car to outrun a man.
Homer!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Huh! What a coincidence. And a perfect opportunity for you to prove your loyalty. Go ahead Bartholomew. You may fire when ready.
A little to the left.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Huh? Oh, very well. You can never be my...
Hey man, I really love your show. I think all kids should watch it. I suddenly feel so dirty.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't know what's happening. It seems our profits have dropped thirty-seven percent.
Thanks, I'd like that.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I get a whiff of the immigrant from these newfangled superheroes.
I wanna stay here with Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I suggest you leave immediately.
I want to stay here with Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I suggest you leave immediately.
But I'm not Homer Simpson...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I think I know who Homer Simpson is. In ten short years you've caused seventeen meltdowns! One is too many!
Why won't you come down?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I told you, I only weigh as much as my clothes and keys!
Mr. Burns, I don't want to seem ungrateful. But, I want to go home to my family.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I was hoping I wouldn't have to tell you this, but... I'm afraid your family doesn't want you back.
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll tell you what day it is. Today is the day you become my heir!
Huh. The light must've burned out.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll thank you to stop pinching my Botticelli.
Then how do you explain this?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've been expecting this day for thirty years. In a way, it's a relief. But in another way, it's most unwelcome.
The world is my ring now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: In this corner, for truth and justice -- Captain Flag and Half-Mast.
He laughed as he heard that old codger's house-sizzles.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Let this be a lesson to those who love cash, that your nice stash of cash could be gone in a flash. And if you are awful and nasty and cruel...
Hey Mr. Burns, did you get that letter I sent?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Letter? I don't recall any letter...
Um, I'd kind of like to go home now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Like a hog! Heh? What? What was that?
Moe, for you... anything?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look! A blue-collar bar! Oh, Smithers, let's go slumming!
We've seen it, dad.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mattingly, for the last time, get rid of those sideburns!
Okay, okay. I'll find you some food.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Me not feel good.
Wow! Swan-ky!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mmmm, delicious. Smithers, every year you outstrip yourself in succulence.
There! Now you don't know which one is Little Monty! I guess if you don't want him to be part of your tuxedo, you'll have to let the other dogs go, too!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nice try. C'mon, Little Monty, stand up!
Oh, Mr. Burns! I'm really sorry!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nonsense, young Woosterfield! Your fortune is greater than mine. It is-it is I who am at your service. Smithers! Fetch us some lemonade!
That explains his mysterious trip to Holland.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now that you've all agreed to reap the windfall of my death, I must return to my large empty mansion to rattle around and await the inevitable... alone.
Sure!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, my dear, if you look in your champagne, I think you'll find a little surprise...
Oh my God. Simon set me up. And all this time I thought he wanted the life of a stranger he met in the bathroom.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, would you care to continue this conversation on the teeter-totter?
Oh man, not the lame-o "Twelve Days of Christmas.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course not! I want to sing the original, unabridged "Thirty-Nine Days Of Christmas". And a one and a two...
That's impossible! How did you get here first?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh well, there'll be plenty of time for explanations later. Right now, I'll be taking my puppies back.
They always told me I was gonna destroy the family, but I never believed it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, don't be frightened of this. It's nothing but a letter opener. Who are you?
For me? But I don't know how to drive.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, pish posh. There's a jaws of life in the trunk.
No, my dog!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, those wheels are squeaking a bit. Perhaps I could sell him a little oil.
Can I go with you to get the treasure? I won't eat much and I don't know the difference between right and wrong.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, you're a good boy. But the child labor people have been watching me like a hawk.
Excellent.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Okay, let's make this sporting, Leonard. If you can tell me why I shouldn't fire you, without using the letter "E," you can keep your job.
It's probably my imagination but something about them didn't seem quite right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Really? Excuse me for just a moment.
Hi. You know, Gramma really likes it when her boyfriends are nice to me. She especially likes it when they give me money.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Run along, Pee-Wee. Baby gets nothing.

Some say the ducks went to Canada. Others say Toronto. And some people think that Joe used to sit down there... near those ducks. But it could be that there's just no room in this modern world for an old man and his ducks.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, do you think maybe my power plant killed those ducks?
You guys don't understand Stampy. He's just like me. We're a pair of jokers and both of us are wild. We don't take nothin' from nobody.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, this reminds me of that fat man I used to ride to work.
Don't stop / Thinkin' about tomorrow! / Don't stop / It'll soon be here...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, we're at war!
No, after twelve.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Tell me, Simpson, if an opportunity arose for taking a small shortcut, you wouldn't be averse to taking it would you?
Don't use that look on me. I invented that look.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There he is, off in the distance!
Yeah, well, anyway, I wonder what he's thinking now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This man is costing my health plan five thousand dollars a day. I demand that he die with dignity.
But what's with the glowing?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Uh, I'll field that question. A lifetime of working in a nuclear power plant has given me a healthy green glow and left me as impotent as a Nevada boxing commissioner. And now that I'm back to normal, I don't bring you peace and love. I bring you fear, famine, pestilence, and...
Shut up... I wanted them to like me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ummm, the child seems rattled.
I wanna hear about old-time wrestling too.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, it looks like you've made a new fan. It'd be a shame to let him down...
You settled that Swede's meatballs!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What I wouldn't give to see Glamorous Godfrey in action once more!
You're preachin' to the choir, man.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What do I have to do? Grow a devil beard?
I'm sorry, Dad... You're fired!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What? Fire me? That does it, you can never be my son...
Prove it, Bony Curtis.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: When the errant bill struck my chest, it left a distinctive bruise. Had my heart been inside at the time, it could have been fatal.
It's a little tight.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, that's to correct your posture. Soon you'll have a mighty hump.
This gun is filled with ketchup. This one with mustard. Now give me three hundred fifty bucks or you're gonna be a mess for your date.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You don't have the guts.
Devon and Quenly?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You don't know when they'll strike -- a boating accident, a mishap during a "ski trip." But rest assured one way or another they will do you in.
I'll do it this afternoon...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You mean there are actually people who will pay good money for garbage?
Yeah, but...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You sold weapons-grade plutonium to the Iraqis! With no mark-up!
Ski trip?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You won't know how they'll strike -- a boating accident...
Healthy. Gettin' healthy. Ow! Gettin' healthy... and very sleepy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahhh. I feel as hail and hearty as an eohippus.
Yeah, you too.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Although this millennium is still young, I feel it is time to award this giant trophy paid for with your healthcare cuts...
Montgomery Burns, you're under arrest for murder.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Did I say corpse-hatch? I meant innocence tube.
Ah, it's too dangerous! Ah-- But I got a sister you might like. She's completely hairless, like those cats.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't care if she's Miss Hairless America... I'm spoken for. Now step aside -- I'll save Gloria myself.
All right, quit stallin', Burns. Who'd you ice?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm afraid that skull belongs to my dear friend... Waylon Smithers, Sr.
I thought that was where they lived!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at those delightful children, Smithers... all those healthy organs, ripe for the harvesting.
Yeah well look a little closer, Lou.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh I hope I'm not too late.
Yeah. Do you think people would be stupid enough to pay for something some amateur put on a wall for nothing?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, no indeed! Now if I can just get my three million dollars back...
Hey, where'd it go? Oh, well.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, there's nothing like canceling an employee drug plan to make one feel so at peace with the universe.
Y-- You? Ah, no offense, but you're a decrepit monkey skeleton.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Perhaps, but this monkey skeleton is in love.
Ahhh. This is the life.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, get me some strike breakers like the kind they had in the 30's.
Cuff him, Lou.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The entire town turned out to jeer me. Me, whose velvet breeches their lizard lips had so often joylessly smooched.
Don't be a fool, Simpson! Let the kid go!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The negotiations have failed! Shoot him!
Remember boys, these are little kids. Take out your tiny batons.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ugh... oh... umph... Oh, Smithers, guide me in.
Take it, Lou.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well hello, Marge. Lovely day for tennis, eh?
So Burns, do you want to explain how this miracle of measure and harmony got into your collection?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I... you see... it's just is it a crime to want nice things? And then to steal them from a public museum where any gum-chewing monkey in a Tufts University jacket can gawk at them? I think not!
That means our murderer could be on the other side of this hatch.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What are you doing in my corpse-hatch?
In a pig's eye he is!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Act your age, Simpson! You look foolish!
That's the activity room. We're not allowed in there. That's the library. Not allowed in there, either. And don't even think about going in the game room...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Egad, man, how are we supposed to pass the time?
Son! You've gotta help me! I hit three people on the way over here, and I don't have any insurance. So, hows 'bout you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent shot, Smithers. I'll be squeezing my Bobo in no time.
Oh, fine. One dinner.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent. So we'll take the boy and make a night of it.
Homer, are you sure you can fly this thing?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Fear not, Smithers. I'll move Heaven and Earth to save you! It's still easier than teaching a new assistant my filing system.
But every unit has a troublemaker. Ours was a cocky little private named Montgomery Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Haven't you won the war yet?
Turn it up! Turn it up!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello, I am Montgomery Burns.
No! Look, take the art if you want. Just don't hurt the boy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm. I'd rather do both.
I don't care! My grandson's soul is at stake!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How dare you! I wrote a song for you! When am I ever going to use that again? Curse you and this morbidly obese little half-wit.
Yeah, yeah... go ahead.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I need that money. Please, please...
Yeah, well, it's your turn to get the ball out of the peach basket.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll get the ball out of your peach basket one of these days.
Aghhh! Don't kill me!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've tried to meet you halfway on this, Simpson, but you had to be Little Johnny Live-a-lot. Now give me your key to the Hellfish Bonanza.
You want me to report ya to Commander Flanders? Just leave 'em, Burnsie.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Leave them for whom? The Germans? The folks who shoot at us all day? Let's just take them. We'll all be rich! Rich as Nazis!
What the hell do you think you're doing?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mr. Simpson, I dread the day when a hundred thousand dollars isn't worth groveling for.
Don't sneak up on a...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No need for the blown gasket, Charlie! I'll have her back in one piece.
Garsh darn it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course. We wouldn't think of going without the bait... uh, that is, the bait-thing beauty -- The bathing beauty. I covered that up pretty well.
I can't remember when I felt this young. I really can't.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Say, sport, mind if I have the next dance?
Over my dead body it will!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's exactly the poi-- Oh, Simpson, can't you go five seconds without humiliating yourself?
Oh yeah--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The world may have despised Glamorous Godfrey, but that conceited mother-puncher was my hero.
Well, I don't feel right about it... but I could use a nest egg for retirement. I'd hate to wind up in one of them old folks homes.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Then it's agreed. Of course, we can't sell the paintings now. We'd be caught. How many of you are familiar with the concept of a "tontine?
I wish this show had a visit from three new writers.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait, what's this? Carpetbags and portmanteaus? Going somewhere, Simpson?
Wait... wait a minute... wait. You're the guy who owns the nuclear power plant.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, the ownership is divided.
That's for others to say now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What are you doing, Godfrey! You're a villain, not some bullet-brained rail-splitter. Without someone to hate, there's no excitement, no thrill!
I ain't gonna kill ya. That'd be cowardly. Monty Burns cowardly. I just wanna watch you squirm.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, sir! Is this to your liking?
Get outta here.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You just made yourself a very powerful enemy, old man.
Sorry, we're not allowed to read newspapers. They angry up the blood.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You! The troublemaking girl!
Go back to being a villain? Forget that! Being hated is the worst feeling there is.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You've got it all wrong, my friend. Once you see it my way, you'll understand that being hated is the greatest feeling in the world.
How long was that?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Your clownish behavior notwithstanding, we have made a gentleman's agreement and sworn on our lives to honor it.
I'll show Grampa. I'll find my own surrogate father, full of heart-warming stories I can share with the world.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ... and that's how you win an opium war!
Well, how 'bout donating money to charity? Lots of crazy old coots do that.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A charitable donation, eh? Well, there's a first time for everything.
You gotta be kiddin'.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A civilian! She mustn't know I'm a hero! Gouge her eyes out!
Bo-ring!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A man who provided the Burns Corporation with forty-five years of faithful service, Mr. Jack Marley.
Me, sir? Oh, no. Not a chance. Only idiots drink beer.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Actually, I was wondering if you'd join me. My treat.
Uh-oh. Usually when it gets this quiet Mr. Burns is standing behind me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Actually, I'm standing in front of you.
Oooh, right next to the boss. Eh, he'll never know who did it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah Simpson! There's someone I want you to meet. Aristotle Amadopolis, owner of the Shelbyville Nuclear Power facility.
MAX POWER / HE'S THE MAN / WHOSE NAME YOU'D LOVE TO TOUCH / BUT YOU MUSTN'T TOUCH / HIS NAME SOUNDS GOOD IN YOUR EAR / BUT WHEN YOU SAY IT, YOU MUSTN'T FEAR / 'CAUSE HIS NAME CAN BE SAID BY ANYONE...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah! Max Power! How's every little thing?
Hired goons?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, Homer! I hope Crusher and Low Blow didn't hurt you.
Nope. Nope. Nope.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, he wouldn't even hear me out.
Uh, they're just snowmen, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, snowmen have peepers. Peepers to watch. To watch for our moment of weakness and then baff! comes the knock on the head and we're down.
Marge, this ticket doesn't just give me a seat, it also gives me the right - no, the duty, to make a complete ass of myself.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, the Gammills. Good to see you.
You mean Maggie?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, the baby who shot me. No, I was referring to your other daughter.
Yeah, out of the way, whoever you are. You're blocking the food.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, there's nothing like a good old-fashioned picnic. How's my kite doing, Smithers?
Uh, uh, just resting my eyes.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, well done. A rested employee is a vigilant employee.
Uh, Smithers already left, Sir. I'm his replacement, Homer Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, yes, Simpson. I'll have my lunch now. A single pillow of shredded wheat, some steamed toast, and a dodo egg.
Stay back! I have powers! Uh, political powers!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah. 206 bones... fifty miles of small intestine... full, pouting lips. Why, this fellow is less a snowman than a god.
Afternoon, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah... Hello, there, uh... uh...
Aren't we getting num-nums?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahh. The solarium. We'll be safely cornered in this glass room with one door.
Nice to meet you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahhh, the new Packard we've been hearing so much about.
Ho, ho, ho, Merry Everyone!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahoy hoy, St. Nick!
Y'ello.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahoy-hoy, executive V.P. I'm putting the final touches on my speech to the investors and I need your generous guffaws.
Take a hike boss, I'm running things now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All hail king Homer!
You can supervise me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, good. Let's dig... That's right, dig some more... Oh, we make quite a duo: Burns and associate. No, no, what am I thinking? Burns and... teammate.
Okay. What I was going to say, was...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, next on my shopping list...a new phone!
Wait a minute. I'm not signing anything until I read it, or somebody gives me the gist of it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, well, it just explains that you've won -- yes, that's it -- won the first annual... uh... Montgomery Burns... uh... Award for... a-a-a Outstanding Achievement in...a-a th... th.. the field of... uh, Excellence!
Well, here we are.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right. Let me start off by telling you this will not be a walk in the park. This will be the most arduous and backbreaking weekend of your life. I cannot overemphasize the dangers which... did you bring your family, Simpson?
Woo-hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All you've got to do is sell fracking to your friends and neighbors.
Would you like me to shred those environmental reports for you, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Already taken care of.
Ooo, Arthur Fortune. You know what that fabulous man just did? He gave the Springfield zoo two male Pandas, and got them to mate successfully.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And a stunt like that impresses people?
You're outta here, drug-o.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And don't forget, federal law mandates that we consider alcohol a drug.
Yes, sir. I do.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And is he a constant disappointment? Does he bring home nitwits and make you talk to them?
Fine.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And now our main event. In this corner: Baby Face Palooka...
Now get out of my house.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And so in the spirit of fence-mending and grudge-not-bearing, I hereby rename the Burns Germ Warfare Lab The Grandma Simpson Peace Museum and Kid-teractive Learnatorium.
I said Wiggum!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And so, potential investors...
Hey, this sounds like fun.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And the last team to arrive will be fired.
But the book said you would applaud my initiative.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And what book is that? The Ape Who Wanted A Big Bonus? Stop wasting my time, you corn-fed man-cow.
GOING UP SHE GOES! UP SHE GOES!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: BALANCE YOURSELF LIKE A BIRD ON A BEAM
Woo-hoo? I don't know... "Fracking" is one of those scary Lisa words.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bah! Fracking produces enough clean natural gas to make America independent of sheikhs, caliphs and... Scandinavians. Not to mention it doesn't create any of that awful worker-mutating nuclear waste.
How come Bart gets to do that and I can't spend one night lurking in the bushes outside Chef Boyardee's house?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bart, I know you children see me as some sort of "booger man," but I'm really not such a bad "dude." Oh, your milk's gone cold. I'll ring for the maid.
Don't mind if I do.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bottoms up Simpson, there's plenty more where that came from.
Umm. Spaghetti.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But Homer, tonight's our reception for Queen Beatrice of the Netherlands.
Bull-honkey! I don't care about joining this stupid club.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But does your wife?
Marge!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But now it's time to say goodbye. Please get off my property until next year. I suggest you don't dawdle. The hounds will be released in ten minutes.
And decrepit.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But you can escape -- and use this map to retrieve my buried treasure. With it, you can have your revenge!
God! It's him!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: C'mon, boys, overpower it!
Twenty eight minutes till Burns comes. Time for operation Mail Take.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Can I help you?
Attention, lovers of free office supplies! Come and steal things you can easily afford!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Can someone open this bottle of mother wolf placenta for me?
Lisa, I don't know what you're doing, but it's very strange and your father is trying to worry.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Chapter the Fifth... A Trip to the Infirmary, With Most Unexpected Results.
These aren't reptile eggs! You've been cheating! No matter where Mr. Burns hits the ball, you put a fresh one on the green!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Cheating for me? Good lord, Smithers, that's patently unnecessary. I'm one of the world's finest golfers! In all the years you've caddied for me, I've never lost a-- Oh.
I need a mouth hole. And some other holes too.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Cheer up, my chubby inner child. I've got a feeling everything's going to work out fine. Because I'VE GOT YOU UNDER MY SKIN...
My favorite is Chicago deep dish.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Chicago, eh? Well what if I took us there now?
Hindu. What do you call the moisture on your Hin?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Classic. Now, tell them how to run a nuclear plant!
Bart! No! No! No, no! Oh no, Bart, No! Don't! Noooo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Close one this year.
No, not him! Anyone but him! I've had my problems with him. Everyone has. But like every monster, he just wants to be loved.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Come on! It's cobblering time!
Not my department.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Curse that Elon Musk! Thanks to that Earth-smooching buttinski, I'm on the verge of bankruptcy. All I have left are the clothes on my back and the clones in my freezer.

Marge likes sushi, I like gum that squirts in your mouth. She's into romantic comedies, I like movies where there's only one day a year when murder is legal. Yep, Marge and I see the world in totally different ways.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Different, exactly. That's why I had to give my woman the old heave-ho.
But I promised my daughter--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Do as I say or I'll tell the police. You'll do so much community service.
I liked when I threw the pudding.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Do it again! I'll make it an even eight.
C'mon, just pick a popular song.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Do you have anything by Prince... Wilhelm of Prussia?
No, ma'am.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Don't worry, Simpson, it just so happens I have a chair at Springfield University...
Sorry, Burns. No deal.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Don't worry, Smithers, he's playing hard ball now. But it won't take him long to crack.
A million dollars and three Hawaiian Islands. Good ones, not the leper ones.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Done. Now, give me that bear.
These would stop Joan Collins herself.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Drat! I wish that song were longer.
Can Lenny have it?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Eh, here's where I stopped checking it last time: September nineteen twenty ni-- Oh, no! Oh, no! Oh, no! Smithers, why didn't you tell me about this market crash?!
Uh... they all won.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Eh? What about my options?
Uh, I'm Homer Simpson, your trusted employee.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Employee, eh? What a pleasant surprise.
Marge, they knew what they were getting into when their parents sold them to the circus.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Enough! You will comport yourself with the dignity expected of a traveling freak show!
That's the sneeze guard. You have to lean under it to get salad or sneeze on stuff.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Everything's so green and alive!
Well, I would like to survive long enough to see the effects of global warming. I've got an inside tip that it's all a bunch of crap. Okay, you've found your snitch.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent! Now, what have you got for me?
Umm... What the hey. I'll take the job.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent! Your first duty will be to step out on the balcony and tell that crowd this plant is safe.
Uh, well okay, what the hey?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent. Set you to your task, Simpson.
Honey, it's me again. I can't work knowing that you're mad at me. I just wanna hear your voice. And I'm counting the minutes till the whistle blows, then I go to Moe's, then I rush home to you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Explain this infernal wheel to me again!
How are you a winner? You're cheating in a fake sport!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Fake? Ridiculous! If professional wrestling were fake... that would make every fan in the history of the sport a complete and utter moron.
Oh yeah, she's always trying to improve mankind.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Fascinating. Do go on.
Take that, Uncle Sam!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Faster, Simpson! Those jack-booted G-men won't be far behind.
I can't believe it! I'm actually running a marathon! Oh, I hit the wall! This is so painful! Hey, I got my second wind. Another wall! I ju-- Woo hoo! Third wind!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Faster, rickshaw driver! Faster!
Well, sir, for one thing we had a problem every Tuesday, when the cafeteria would serve fish sticks.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Fish sticks? What in blazes are you talking about?
Uh, Mr. Burns, I'd like you to meet... Mother Hubbard standee.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: From the Wisconsin Standees! Milk-fed, yet so slim. Permit me to play you a tune on my mouth organ.
Hello, Mr. Burns? This is your mother.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Gah! Oh, hello, Mater. Uh... Sorry about pulling the plug on you and all. Who could've known you'd pull through and... live for another five decades? Oh, is my face red...
Woo-ooo! I'm a work of art! "Last Supper", eat your heart out!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Garbage! What matchbook art school did you flunk out of, you ham-fisted, nearsighted house painter? Smithers, throw this on the dung heap.
Eww. I touched it. Over.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Get a grip, Simpson. You're doing fine. Now, do you have your map?
But I think the dodo went extinct...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Get going! And answer those phones, install a computer system, and rotate my office so the window faces the hills.
I can see why this is so popular.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Give me my bear, Simpson.
It seems to be stuck. Bad baby! Bad Maggie!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Give me the bear!
Who?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Glamorous Godfrey was the most famous wrestler in the world! And you are he!
Oh my God! Oh my God! Oh my God!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Gloria, say you'll marry me.
Mr. Burns! The Nuclear Regulatory Commission is here for a surprise inspection!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good Lord! That canary was supposed to be my pigeon. I need to find a patsy quick!
I think I'm blind.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good day to you.
Nobody loves you...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good heavens, Smithers! They're not afraid of me anymore!
Just my luck.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good lord, Smithers! You look atrocious. I thought I told you to take a vacation.

You know what, Mr. Burns? I'm never comin' back. My son's making so much cash in the T-shirt game, that I don't have to work another day in my life -- assuming my health does not deteriorate as I age.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good riddance to bad blubber. Smithers, want to go get a cup of coffee?
You know, Mr. Burns, my family and I feel that taxes are too high. Where do you stand on this highly controversial issue?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Goodness! I didn't realize this casual dinner was going to turn into a charged political debate.
Oh come on, she's a little girl.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Grow a spine on your own time, Blimpo.
There must have been a mistake. My body is a temple.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Guards! Remove this coked-out man balloon from my sight!
Echo, echo...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: HEY DON'T YOU REMEMBER / THEY CALLED ME AL / IT WAS AL ALL THE TIME / HEY DON'T YOU REMEMBER / I'M YOUR PAL / BUDDY, CAN'T YOU SPARE A DIME.
Marge, kids.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Have you people forgotten our little competition? Last one in the cabin is fired.
Mr. Burns! Where's Mr. Smithers?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: He's doing eighty years on an opium bust. I never saw a man take to a Turkish prison so quickly.

Okay book, I didn't read you, and you didn't read me, but we're both in this together, so say something smart or get ready to run like hell. Um... "In business as in breakfast, fried eggs have fragile yolks... huh, huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: He's got them eating out of his hand. And to think you doubted him, Smithers.
Sorry, no can do!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hear me out, Simpson. I don't want you to come back as a Technical Supervisor, or Supervising Technician, or whatever the hell you used to do. I want you to be in charge of safety here at the plant.
No you don't. Heh, heh.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Heh, heh, heh. Heh, heh. Ohh, you'll find this amusing -- the suit Charlie Chaplin was buried in.
Dad says this new guy is a repulsive, obnoxious old billionaire, so let's all be extra-nice to him.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello! Why it's... it's uh... oh it's...
Yeah, well I'll be on my --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello, there's more. "In case you can't tell, I'm being sarcastic...
Bo-ring!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello. My name is Mr. Snrub, and I come from... eh, someplace far away. Yes, that will do. Anyway, I-I say we invest that money back in the nuclear plant.
But I haven't finished my rituals yet!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Help! I'm wafting on a zephyr!
Ewww!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Here's a scoop for your readers: the Hall of Patriots.
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Here's your caption, boys: "Local Hero shuns spotlight and pitches in!
Oh, man. Plain cake donuts? Thanks for taking all the fancies, guys. Why can't I ever get here on time?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hi, ho, faceless employees. In a few moments the government inspection team will be touring your plant so look busy and keep your mouths shut. That is all.
G-g-g-g-hags!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hm, looks like it's pledge day. Which jailhouse fraternity shall I join?
John Denver.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm, that's odd. Usually the blood gets off at the second floor.
I'm just trying to work up the courage to ask Burns for a raise. Or a highly-paid internship. Something to solve my money woes.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm, this must be some sort of cafetorium.
Well, I'm no Carl when it comes to this stuff. But I ain't no Lenny neither. And I would say... no matter how much you try to keep things casual, someone always gets hurt.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm... Well then I must harden my heart against such an outcome.
Uh, I'm sorry, Mr. Burns, but you can't have these dogs. Am I fired?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm? Oh, of course not. They're your pets, you can do as you wish. Good day, everyone.
Enjoy your tartar sauce, boys! Enjoy! Give me your plates. Don't crowd. Plenty for everybody.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmmm. Brilliant. Who could have ever imagined that Simpson's sweeping reforms would pay off so quickly?
Will you shut up, I'm trying to think of a name.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmmm. Crude, but I like it. What do you say we freshen up our little drinkie poos?
It could be days before they find us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmmm... no books, no radio, no board games. Ah! A Bazooka Joe comic.

Well, listen to me, Mr. Bigshot... if you're looking for the kind of employee who takes abuse and never sticks up for himself... I'm your man. You can treat me like dirt and I'll still kiss your butt and call it ice cream. And if you don't like it... I can change!!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hold the phone, Smithers... I like your attitude. Feisty yet spineless.
I was only reading what the card...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Homer, I agree with you and, if I'm elected governor, I will lower taxes whether those bureaucrats in the State capital like it or not.
Damn right!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Homer, I want you to show this woman the time of her life.
Wait a minute! There's probably a --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Homer, your bravery and quick thinking have turned a potential Chernobyl into a mere Three-Mile Island. Bravo!
He likes you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How dare you destroy my valuable wall and spill my priceless acid?! Did you really think you were going to get away with it?
Hep... heyyy... whoooo... look out... yeah... Da da da da da.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How does he do it, Smithers?
I knew you'd come crawling back.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How much do you want?
Uh uh.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: However, I can take that off by dusting my hands thusly.
What's that, sonny?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Huh... This is all so sudden...
Uh... Simp-sons, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Huh? Hmmm, oh, oh yes... Homer and Marge Simpson. Oh, and these must be Bart, Lisa and uh, "Expecting".
And it's important to feel good about yourself... Okay, spread your toes. Do you know how much glass is in here?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hurry, Smithers. Halloween is upon us. Put up the decoration.
Uh, this is Eduardo, my pool boy. He thinks he's an angry rich man.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I am an angry rich man!
I don't know... a hundred and two?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I am only eighty-one. You may find this hard to believe... but in my salad days, my crowning glory was a bright shock of strawberry blond curls.
Oops, no time for that now -- the computer's starting.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I am pleased to dedicate this remote work terminal. It will allow our safety inspector here to perform his duties from home. And so, excelsior to you, Mr. What's the name of this gastropod?
Well, you can either get up or go back to sleep.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I believe I'll get up.
Text me the choices.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I can't believe I'm on the town with Glamorous Godfrey himself! Tell me of your epic battle with Swedish Olaf Johannsen.
Will you keep giving me money?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I can't have my little monkey running around in rags.
Goodnight and good gravy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't think so.
Well, sir... you see, sir... I've worked here a long time, and my wife has a game leg, and my kids have game things as well...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't want to hear your whining. I'm a bored and joyless old man, give me a laugh!
Well, I won't sleep in the same bed with a woman who thinks I'm lazy. I'm gonna go right down stairs, unfold the couch, unroll a sleeping bag... Eh, goodnight.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I dreamed about her again last night, Smithers. You know that dream where you're in bed and they fly in through the window?
Wayne, stop! That's Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I expect insolence, but rank insolence? Off with his job!
I'm bald!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I had but one item left on the list... "A picture of myself with a smiling child." What could be easier?
Well... one.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I have embarked on a "beneficial friendship" with a woman with whom I have nothing in common. Her opinions are abhorrent to me. But the passion... well, look at these racy texts she sends me.
I'VE BEEN SITTIN' ON THE TOILET / ALL THE LIVE-LONG DAY...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I hope no one finds out about this. It's pure journalistic dynamite!
Uh, yeah, sure. That thing.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I hope you don't mind a little walking.
Charge! I mean, yes sir?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I just bought a new car. A nice foreign number... the Lamborgotti Fasterossa.
Well, sir, they cut the head off a fish and chop up the rest into sticks, and then put seasoned bread crumbs on them.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I know what fish sticks are! Get to the point!
Bad dog! Bad neighbor dog! Here, let me help you up, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I love dogs... babies, too.
Marge, get my gun.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I must have her. Smithers, zoom in. Closer... Closer... closer, damn it!
Yes, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I said her. And I said knee.
...having only one pancake leaves room for more bacon.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I see what you're saying. We're crowding your plate. In fact, there's no need for us to be here at all. Let's go, Smithers.
So lazy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I see. Well, I... Oh, you know, I just remembered it's time for my annual donation. I wonder how much I should give...
Oh, I hope I haven't upset you... bongo head!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I should be resisting this, but I'm paralyzed with rage... and island rhythms.
Just what are you guys up to?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I suppose there's no harm in telling you. I'm using the rocket to dispose of Springfield's nuclear waste -- by sending it straight to the heart of the Amazon rainforest!
Well, I'm still gonna run!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want the whole world to hear the story of my harrowing struggle with hypohemia.
Why does he always bring up my weight?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want you to eliminate this reporter: Kent Brockman. He found the gully where I dump electricity every summer to jack up prices.
I see. Well, I'll need some beer.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want you to look at me the way I saw you look at Arthur Fortune.
But I can't find you funny anymore.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll either tickle your ribs or feed them to my dogs! Now we're ordering out. What would you like on your pizza pie? Extra cheese?! Who do you take me for? Lorenzo De Medici?
Hold on a minute. Governor, I've been using my powers of snitching for evil. But now I want to tattle for good. This prison is a hellhole. They feed us horse meat -- with traces of jockey meat!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll have you know I buy the finest cuts of beef.
Me? But that's you!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll pick you up at five tomorrow. And I'll pick you up right now.
Thanks for giving me my old job back.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm afraid it's not that simple. As punishment for your desertion, it's company policy to give you the plague.
No pink box?! Wha -- what's going on?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm afraid your daily donuts are no more.
Oh, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm going to make such love to you that, oh, you'll forget all about Rudolph Valentino. Turn left here.
Oh, Marge.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm going to write a figure on this piece of paper. It's not quite as large as the last one, but I think you'll find it fair.
Mr. Burns!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm so sorry, Mr. Burns. I won't disturb you again.
Now the movie's turned into a play! Still good, though.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm sorry I lied to you, Waylon, but I wanted to spare you the details of your father's gruesome death.
Where did you come from?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm your cellmate. You never noticed me, because, frankly, you're extremely self-centered.
Mom, there's nothing to be alarmed about, but could you take one last look at the family and join me in the kitchen?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've been waiting twenty-five years for this moment.
Sure it will. All we need is a pilot!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've got everything you need.
Bart, please. Five bucks for a kiss.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've never seen such an obvious attempt to curry my favor.
Got it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: If I want you to bunt, I will touch my belt buckle not once, not twice, but thrice...
Aw, don't cry.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: If it makes you feel worse, I'm the man who bought the stock you sold.
Ooh, a movie! I call the couch!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: If you see only one film this year that proves my innocence, make it this one.
Uh... yes sir. I thought I was supposed to.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Imbecile. Simpson, your family will have to remain here.
I already work for you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: In addition to working in your normal capacity at the plant, you will also serve as my personal hit man.
Can I have some ice cream? I finished my pizza.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: In time, in time. I need to speak with you in private.
Beautiful. We have confirmation.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Is everything ready for the secret meeting, Smithers?
Hello. Mr. Burns' office.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Is it about my cube?
Outfoxed 'im with the corpse of my best friend. Hee-hee.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Is there room in the head bag, Smithers?
You're going to ask her to marry you?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Isn't it wonderful? I'm head over heels in love.
I want to buy a pony.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Isn't that cute? Smithers, he's planning on joining the horsey set. That is it, isn't it? You're not planning to eat it?
You got it, buddy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Isn't there any way out of here?
Huh? Wha...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It seems Ari's been having terrible worker problems at Shelbyville.
Do I have to hang out with them?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It would be nice.
Fine, I'll come clean.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's a Christmas miraculum!
Mr. Burns, you do this personally?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's a hobby. I'm not in this for any personal gain, heavens no. By the way, are you acquainted with our state's stringent usury laws?
Uh... Marge, why don't I catch us some salmon?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's about time. We've been making small talk about Mussolini for fifteen minutes.
There sure is. Kids, you tried your best and you failed miserably. The lesson is, never try. Right in the butt. That was great.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's no use. I guess I'll have to leave all my money to the Egg Advisory Council. Eggs have gotten quite a bad rap lately, you know, Smithers.
One... two... Eh, I'd rather die.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's no use. We've got to make an emergency landing.
Well... I don't know.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's the only way you'll survive in here.
It won't happen again, sir. I promise. May I get out of your sight now?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just a second, Simpson! Smithers, would you leave the room for a minute?
The last thing I understood in that was "pants.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just give me your answer! And make it quick! Our current "account man," Robert Marlowe here, is retiring at the end of the month.
What do I do now?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just lean into it. It'll be over soon, one way or another.
Let go of her or I'll scream!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Kaloo-kalei! We're in luck! They had a magnum at the shoe counter. Now for... Gloria?
I don't know why you're trying to steal the plant back. I don't even want it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Keep begging. You're just wasting precious oxygen!
Per... our... agreement!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Knock-kneed home renters. Can't we thin this herd with some smallpox-infected blankets?
And who's selling the uranium to the terrorists? Montgomery Burns. Now, we wait.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Let go of me! I'm innocent!
Well, she's into Buddhism, whistle-blowing, totally against pollution no matter what I say...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Liberal whacko, eh? Any young beaux?
I'll figure it out. I'm gonna use all the power of my brain.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look Smithers! Garbo is coming!
Unlike most of you, I am not a nut. Just a good, honest American who opposes wrongdoing and especially carelessness wherever they occur.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at that man. He has the crowd in the palm of his hand. Haven't seen anything like it since Jolson. Who is he?
By the way, rhyming Homer with Homer...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at them, Smithers, enjoying their embezzlement.
Well, okay then... Four o'clock... Coupla hours I have to get up and go to work... gotta go to work... go to work.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at them, Smithers. Goldbrickers, lay-abouts, slug-a-beds...
Agreed.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at them. Smug and secure in their finery. Mocking us.
We really appreciate that.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at those eyes! There's an employee with a healthy case of the go-get-'ems!
Uh, Murphy, you are elf a controllably I think a we nam- myo-renge-kyo.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look at those two inseparable chums, Smithers. That's exactly the teamwork we'd like to showcase at this year's Energy Convention.
Over my dead body!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look, Smithers... crackle-berries! Spot me a federal, will you?
You know, Bart, when I was your age, I pulled a few boners, but I think you'll find that people are pretty decent if you give them half... Oh, oh.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look, there it is! The head!
Stop that dog! It has my gum!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look, there's one of my young chums now. You there!
Yes sir. Reject the first offer. Reject the first offer.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: May I offer you a drink?
Oh, what do they want!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Maybe a nap will boost my spirits.
All right!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Memorandum to: Mrs. Bouvier. Re: Delineation of Romantic Intentions..." Pfffft, too sappy. Smithers, come over here and help me write a mash note to my girlfriend!
Stop telling them it was me. I'll kill you for saying it was me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mersimp... Son... what is the... mer... meaning of this? Smithers, who is this beast that's shaking me?
Yes, lotta hysteria...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mmm-hmm. If you can take advantage of a situation in some way, it's your duty as an American to do it. Why should the race always be to the swift or the Jumble to the quick-witted? Should they be allowed to win merely because of the gifts God gave them? Well, I say, cheating is the gift Man gives himself.
Don't you care about your son? This is more important than money!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: More important than money? Who is this?
Well, you picked a perfect time to start.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Musicians, cease that infernal tutlitating. "Thank you all..." "...for coming.
Just a little more.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My Gloria is still inside! Save her!
Here's your package, Mr. Burns!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My name is the return address, you senseless dunderpate! Smithers, who is this nincompoop?
C'mon! All we need is a grand slam.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My one game of the year... ruined by pathetic incompetence.
Or what? You'll release the dogs? Or the bees? Or the dogs with bees in their mouths, and when they bark, they shoot bees at you? Well go ahead, do your worst.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My worst, eh? Smithers, release the robotic Richard Simmons.
Uh, not as such.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Neither would I. I've always felt that there's far too much hysteria these days about so-called "cheating".
Wow, Mr. Burns, how did you do that?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Never forget, Homer, there's no muscle stronger than the human heart.
I'll keep my promise, honey.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No looking at pictures of loved ones!
Burns, you're coming with us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No! No! Let me go! Let me go!
Mr. Burns, is there anything at all I can do for you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, Homer. You've already done more for me than any man. Your brutal attack forced me to fend for myself. I realize now that being waited on hand and foot is okay for your average Joe, but it's not for me. I want to thank you.
We could build snowmen.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, I have a better idea! We could build real men. Out of snow.
Gotcha. Marge, we're gettin' some drive-thru then we're doin' it twice.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, I've got something even more special in mind.
I did! Whoo-hoo! Whoo-hoo! In your face, Strawberry!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, Smithers. I've decided to bring in a few ringers. Professional baseballers.
You mean a Van Dyke?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, a Van Dyke has a mustache, doesn't it?
So what do we do with our friend here? Uh, throw him in the dumpster?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no, no, I really want to give the lovable scamp a good home.
I'm really sorry I hit you, Mr. Burns. Here, let me put some salt on that eye.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, please! I can't bear another thrashing. Just leave me be.
Katharine Hepburn?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, you fool. 'Tis I, Burns! Now come with me.
Oh, you mean Tennessee?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. The island of San Glucose. Good times.
Ohhh. Well, if someone of your stature can enjoy a beer, maybe I'm all turned around on the subject. Wait a minute, we're not having a drug test tomorrow, are we?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. Vendor, two, please.
We'll hide out at my place. I've got beer.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No. We need help. And there's only one man who can get us out of a jam like this.
Well, can I at least drive you home, Mr. Burns? It's five o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No... I thought... I thought, uh, I'd chauffeur myself this evening! Yes, that's what I thought. How difficult can it be? I'm sure the manual will indicate which lever is the velocitator and which the deceleratrix.
So you don't miss that politics lady at all?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not for one Chinese second! And I'm sure she's forgotten all about me.
The answer is no, Mr. Burns. Not for any amount of money.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not for one million dollars?
Wait, Mr. Burns! I'm here to man up -- it was all my wife's fault! Sometimes I think she and I have nothing in common.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nothing in common, eh? Tell me more...
And I looked so good on that box.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now Doctor, I want you to test me for everything. Every disease on this chart.
Thank you, Mr. Burns. It was pretty scary up there. But... For a while I feared for my life.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now Homer, if there's anything else I can do for you, please don't hesitate to ask.
I knew it!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now I would like to sing our National Anthem.
What! Oh thank you, thank you, thank you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now get out of here before I reconsider.
Mr. Burns, I think we can trust the President of Cuba.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now give it back.
Nooo! Not community service -- I can't stand helping others! I just can't!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now open the folder. It contains your next victim.
Robots... trying to kill me... and now they'll kill you... 'cause I led them here...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now see here! You are so not the heartless automatons I was looking for! There's one thing man has that machines can never match: hounds!
Nothing you can say will diminish this honor.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now that I'm the town's oldest man, I'm starting to realize I'm not a young man anymore. I'll have to start taking better care of myself. You know, I haven't had a medicino checkup in ages.
Can do.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now there's nothing to do now but sit back and wait for the kudos to roll in.
Now Lisa, I'm an entertainer. And you can't entertain and inform at the same time. And if you're Access Hollywood, you do neither!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now they're all excellent choices, so simply pick the white male candidate you prefer and we'll elect him.
Uh...the last one.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now! As an attack dog, you'll be expected to neutralize intruders.
Awww.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, Homer, you were about to say something to me...
You see white people have names like "Lenny," whereas, black people have names like "Carl.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, Mr. Rude, I just want you to know I'm a good sport. If you want to make fun of my legendary love of cashews, you have at it.
But the note was asking you to --

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, now, now. Tell my secretary I said you could have a free apple. She'll make everything all right, I promise.
Mr. Burns, I've thought about it, and I don't wanna be a snitch. It's not an honorable life.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, now, there are perks. A private cell, extra dessert... and this adorable little hat.
Well, if that's your custom.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, tell me more about your daughter. And speak into the lamp.
Well, at least we're all in this together.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, we have three parachutes.
This is wonderful.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, why don't you listen to the musical stylings of Mr. Lionel Richie.
A P-P-P-P-P-Private jet!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, would you care for some sushi?
Well... Uh... Wine 'em, dine 'em, bring 'em flowers, write 'em love poetry, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Of course! It's simplicity itself! I won't forget this, Simpson. Now return to your work, and tell no one of what transpired here.
But I really can't tell them anything, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh cut the false modesty, it's getting tiresome. Besides, it's your duty. Employee of the Month isn't all ham and plaques.
Svetlana! Svetlana!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh hush! Now let's enjoy the Miami of Canada -- Chicago!
I didn't wake up. It's all a dream. It's just a dream!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh that's right. It's all a dream.
Good one, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh well, I used to rile the late, great Connie Mack with that one at old Shibe Park.
You know, you could have just called me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh yes, but the telephone is so impersonal. I prefer the hands-on touch you only get with hired goons.
Mr. Burns, as team captain, it's my duty to inform you that...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I almost forgot. I brought you all a little something.
I'll tell you what I think. I think he thinks I'm an idiot. The only reason he's offering us this is because he knows he's gonna lose the trial and have to pay us a cool million.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I feel faint..
Uhmmmm... Errr... Uhhhhh...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I get it. I'm on to you.
Wha-- oh, oh, uh, Mr. Burns? Uh, you were cool too.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I so believe that.
Hello, Young man Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, Simpson. You do know how to whip my buggy.
And you wanted to take him to the hospital.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, and you didn't? Well, the worm has finally shown his fangs. Smithers, make me slap him.
You can't win us back with mere donuts.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, but these aren't just any donuts. These donuts were made the old-fashioned way: the dough is sweetened with Cuban sugar from pre-Batista plantations, then it's deep fried in the tallow of three different animals, two of which are now extinct.
Don't correct the man, Brat. Oh, Boss, look what we brought... gelatin desserts.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, for the love of Peter! That's all anybody brought. Some damn fool went around telling everyone I love that slimy goop. Well, toss it in the pile over there.
A laugh? Okay, let's see, what's in the news today...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, for the love of... Hurl this at that.
You know, I was just telling the wife that if I was governor, I'd do things a lot differently.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, get off your soapbox, Simpson! Do you realize how much it costs to run for office? More than any honest man can afford.
Mr. Burns, I've made a list of recommendations to improve plant efficiency.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, have you now? Well huzzah, huzzah. I'll just throw back my legs and pollute my britches with delight.
Disregard.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, he's the worst yet! That's it! Everyone out! Except you! One step to the left.
Then how do you explain this?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, hello Smithers! Fancy seeing you in Casual Encounter Park.
I'm Class President.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, hot dog! Say...how would you like to work for me?
If you really love Larry, prove it and you can have him back today.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, how much proof do you need? Five thousand? Six thousand? I swear, that's all I've got.
Uh, Mr. Burns, couldn't we patch the leak tomorrow? It's date night.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, indeed it is. Tonight I will be continuing my courtship of Princess Wilhelmina of Prussia.
Can you believe I'm a size four? Woo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, it's pointless hunting for an animal that has 24 miles of water to hide in. Drain the lake.
You mean duke it out?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, no, I mean I'm prepared to offer you a most generous cash settlement.
Are you all right, Mr. Burns?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, of course. A little roughhousing with the pets is good for a man's appetite.
Can I leave, Mr. Burns?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, of course. And don't worry, there'll be plenty of apples for you. Nobody will take away your precious apples.
Well, you could treat me with a little respect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, shut up, you tub of guts.
W-well... It's a v-very generous offer, sir. But... his medical bills alone...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, so extortion is the name of your little game, is it Simpson? Very well. Then you get nothing. I have the finest lawyers in Springfield, Simpson. Tangle with me and I'll crush you like a paper cup.
Honey, I'm home!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, there's an original sentiment.
Do I get paid now?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, where are my manners? There.
Mr. Burns, I, uh, was wondering if you'd like to sponsor my bowling team... for five hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, why, certainly, Pop 'n Fresh. I... I owe my robust physique to your tubes of triple-bleached goo.
What do we do?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, wouldn't you like to know.
You know, Mr. Burns, you're the richest guy I know. Way richer than Lenny.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes, but I'd trade it all for a little more.
Oh, these sure are comfortable chairs.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, yes, sitting. The great leveler. From the mightiest Pharaoh to the lowliest peasant, who doesn't enjoy a good sit?
Two in a row!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, you've really turned my life around these past few weeks, Lisa. I've got my own business again, my beloved employees... oh consargnit. Eh, come on, let's pick up the pace, you neglected old nincompoops!
Hey, that guy looks like you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh-ho, that's me all right, standing up against America's reckless, spendthrift politicians. It commemorates my liberation of a trillion dollars that would have been foolishly squandered.
Which way to the bathroom?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh. It's the twenty-third door on the left.
I love spying.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ohh, don't worry about those fumes. They'll be sucked into that air vent.
Gee, sorry, Dave.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Okay, going down the checklist: feu allumé...oui. Ballon gonflé, oui.
Marge! Don't worry. My daughter's very bright, I'm sure she'll be able to memorize your question by dinner time tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Only an innocent child could get away with such blasphemy. God bless them all. Amen.
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, I'm afraid you misunderstand. This picnic is for me. You will all be spending your Independence Day slaving away in the hot summer sun without pay, lotion or gratitude.
Well, why do I have to do the Lindy Hop?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ooh, that's the heart of the bit!
THIS IS THE SONG THAT YOU HEAR AT THE CIRCUS / SUNG BY A GUY THAT YOU SEE AT THE CIRCUS...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Or gape in terror at Almighty God's whoopsy-daisies...the Freaks!
Now I have nothing.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Perhaps I may be of help.
I gotta go shake the dew off the lilly.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Perhaps you're wondering why you have two heads? Well my body was crushed so I had my head grafted on to or shall we say ample frame.
Do you really think you can capture the Loch Ness Monster? I mean, he's eluded Leonard Nimoy and Peter Graves.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Peter Graves couldn't find ugly at a Radcliffe mixer!
Ummm...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Play along, Chubsy. There's a pie in it for you.
Uh... Mr. Burns... I need to borrow some money.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Please, do go on...
And I'll be right here watching TV.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Poke-A Poke-A Poke-A! Poke-A Poke-A Poke-A!
Uh... Excuse me, Mr. Burns?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pop 'n Fresh! You glutinous little doughboy! Oh, there's something I've wanted to do to you for years.
Hey, I called for that!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Put a lid on it, Simpson. There's no "I" in "team".
I'll handle it. I always do.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Rafting, eh? It's a perfect way to entertain them. Finally, humanity has found a use for water.
Yeah! Especially your big fat... Oh, wait.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Raise your right hock. Aerate! Raise your left hock. Aerate! I want to see more Teddy Roosevelts and less Franklin Roosevelts!
Good morning, Mr. Burns. Beautiful day to be outside, isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Rant on, Simpson, but your vainglorious boasting will only add savor to my inevitable triumph.
Heh, heh. Taft, you old dog...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Really, Smithers, I'll be fine! I'm sure your replacement will be able to handle everything. Who is he, anyway?
Bart!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Remember, your job and the future of your family hinges on your successful completion of Nuclear Physics 101.
Burns' Mansion?! That's Mr. Burns' mansion!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Remind me, Smithers: while we're out, I need to get my eyes re-balled and my brain flushed out with vinegar.
What are you doin'?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Scream all you like, no one will hear you!
Say it Burns. Say I never shot you... Before.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shot? By you? I'm afraid not my primitive friend. Your kind has neither the cranial capacity nor the opposable digits to operate a firearm. The one who shot me was...
Uh, Mr. Burns... Uh, Mr. Burns...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shut up and wreck something.
Please, Mr. Burns, pretend you work for me. You can have the boy, just don't beat him. You can beat him, just don't leave marks.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Shut up, you waste of skin and fat! You've desecrated my every possession!
It's not a rubber band, it's a scrunchie!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silence! Or I'll chop you into suet for my murderous gerbils and hamsters.
What are you doing here? I told you I'm not your monkey anymore.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silence, Monkey. Now that you're Father Christmas, we have an opportunity to bend this town over our knee and give it a pranking it will never forget. Here's what we do...
U-su-ry?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silly me, I must have just made up a word that doesn't exist. Now, what is the purpose of this loan?
Hey, you know boys, a nuclear reactor's a lot like a woman. You just have to read the manual and press the right button.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson -- Monty Burns. Come with me.
You're not a client. You're the client.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson! Put on your charm-their-pants-off pants! The mumpish oafs in Washington are sending their sternest band of nuclear regulators, handpicked to resist all blandishment.
How did you ever run this place? You've gotta turn away your family, fire your friends, work until the wee hours of the afternoon...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, I worked here for three-score and twain. That's sixty-two years in the "New English". Now, come with me, I want to show you something.
Uh... Mr. Burns, in spite of what everybody thinks, I'm no lover-boy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, I'm asking you nicely.
Homer Simpson, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, eh? Hmm hmmm. I'm Monty Burns.

Mr. Burns, before I leave, I've got a few things to get off my chest: one: I liked the new microwave in the break room -- just push "popcorn". You don't have to know how long.
