Two: replacing us with robots is heartless and despicable. Three: how about a farewell party with a caricature artist? You know, it's something both kids and adults can enjoy. So to sum up: nicely-done, we hate you, and food for thought.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, wait! As it turns out, there is one job available. But be forewarned, it promises naught but soul-crushing boredom.
I was in so deep, I forgot pies were food.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson, you're late, bald and stupid! I'm docking you a day's pay.
Same here.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson. I want you to rejoin our power plant family.
It's my first day.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Since I've never seen you before, maybe it is your first day. Very well, carry on.
Can't talk now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! I don't want that unpredictable lunatic working in my casino!
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I'm beginning to think that Homer Simpson was not the brilliant tactician I thought he was.
Woo hoo! Problem solved!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I've designed a new plane. I call it the Spruce Moose, and it will carry two hundred passengers from New York's Idlewild Airport to the Belgian Congo in seventeen minutes.
Hey, Barney, look. It was on my list, along with a lot of other things I didn't get to do today. Hey, my boss!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, check out the luscious pair on that red-head. That's it, baby. Work those ankles.
My secret shame.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, my plan worked perfectly. Bart Simpson will live here as my son, and I will mold him in my own graven image. Who knows, I may even grow to love him. Bartholomew!
More of what?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, the hounds feel terrible for what they did. And good news, one pooped out your ear! We'll dip it in iodine and it's just like new.
Yes... but I've got a friend who owes me a solid.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, who is this barrel-chested go-getter?
I'm not your buddy, you greedy old reptile!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, who is this saucy fellow?
I've never been so happy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, why haven't I heard of this "The Leader?" He's as rich and wicked as I, but he seems to enjoy tax exempt status.
He is not my boyfriend!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So Simpson, I hear you like pizza pie.
Oh, the Patriot Act is so terrible! The government might find out what library books I take out. What's next -- finding out what operas I go to?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So it's agreed: we cancel the rest of the primaries and offer the G.O.P. nomination to this knee-high want-wit.
Well, I am a sucker for a little hat.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So we have an agreement?
A must!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So we need one meat sock on the payroll. But who?
Then, I insert this old videotape of us working on a continuous loop...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, another Friday is upon us. What'll you be doing, Smithers? Something gay, no doubt.
But Mr. Burns, it's not my bear. It's Maggie's.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, good sand today, hm.
No, it's entirely within my power. Furthermore, there never were any nuclear inspectors. Check and mate. Now, king me!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, the caterpillar has emerged from its cocoon as a shark with a gun for a mouth. I only have one thing to say to that... bravo.
Was on fire. Was. I finally get a job I was good at, and now I have to give it up.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, you've come begging not to be fired? Smithers, turn my back on this man. Maximum huff!
--son!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Sounded large when I ordered it. I can't make hide nor hair of these metric booby-traps.
You don't understand... my son just threw his red hat in with the white laundry...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Spare me the tired semantics of the Simpson family! Take him away!
Thank you, Mr. Burns. Thank you for... huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Steal my plant will you? By the time you wake up, you'll be walled inside my mausoleum forever!
They made us!" That's loser talk! You gotta start acting more like me and my team, the future league champions of the world! Nothing's gonna stop us now!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Stop everything! I don't remember writing a check for bowling!
You really blew it this time, Smithers.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Stop that! Stop that at once! You're fighting!
Be my guest, but I seriously doubt the old man ever reads 'em.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Suggestion eight thousand, four thirty-two: Nix!
These guys aren't so tough. I've got "Wonder Bat.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Take a knee boys.
She's right. Yes, I may be naked and reeking of panda love, but I've got to stop this before it goes too far.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Take that back for nine hundred and three dollars.
Homer Simpson has become a snitch.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Tell me something I don't know.
Thank you, mysterious weirdo.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Tell me, what student government office do you hold? Secretary? Treasurer? Dare I say Secretary-Treasurer?
Yes, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Tell my young sweetheart here of our youthful exploits.
I hope it's spaghetti!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank you, and goodbye.
AND COULD I LEAVE YOU / RUNNING MERRILY THROUGH THE SNOW?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That beautiful voice! It's making my heart race!
Not funny. And the one in my pants really hurt.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That man who's getting all those laughs, Smithers. Who is he?
That's right. And as my first act... Mr. Burns, you're fired!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That man's mad. Smithers, get this bedlamite an alienist!
Can I keep him anyway? Huh, huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That was delightful! Did you see that? That mouse butchered that cat like a hog! Is all TV this wonderful?
That's all well and good, but it's not really your idea, is it now Marge?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's it. Frimble about with your widgets and doobobs. It'll all be a monument to futility when my plan comes to fruition.
The Dalai Lama!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's right. All his talk of peace and love is really honking off my red Chinese masters. Now Smithers, walk me around the park until I fall asleep. I'm feeling fussy.
Oh, great stuff. And the life lesson is...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The Yangtze River swallows all secrets.
Ugh, ah, hello, Mr. Burns. Would you like to watch the fight?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The fight? Don't mind if I do. Oh, Simpson. Good news -- I brought some munchies. Smithers -- the Cheetos.
Safety? But, sir, if truth be known, I actually caused more accidents around here than any other employee. There were even a few doozies no one ever found out about.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The generous offer I'm making is good for exactly thirty seconds, Simpson.
It's all here, and it's all backwards. That's right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The world has turned has it not my tin-plated friend? Look at you -- you, who were once so proud -- Feel the wrath of the left hand of Burns!
Thanks, Charlie. Maybe fracking isn't so bad.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Then say yes to this raise, this promotion, and this flannel shirt which says "I'm not screwing you over!
No. There's no way out.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There must be some way to contact the outside world. Ah, the telegraph.
A little too well, if you ask me. I'm sure he's plotting some brilliant scheme to get those puppies.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There you go. There you go. You too...
All right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: They say you catch more flies with honey. I say with flytraps!
Well, ah, I wish the candy machine wasn't so picky about taking beat-up dollar bills... because a lot of workers really like candy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This is my park! Get out!
Hello!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This moon-faced simpleton is continually interrupting my search for a patsy! Hello.
Where are we going, sir?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: To create a new and better world.
Maybe for you. How come you didn't rescue me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Too busy trying to keep my sides from splitting -- it's happened before. Monty say, monkey do. What could be better?
Hi, Mr. Burns. Do you want your coffee now?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Uh... no! I'm... uh... making it myself!
You... can't... do that...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Until Mr. Roosevelt's New Deal starts working, this country's still in a depression. I'm spending a fortune on atoms, and we have to cut costs!
Uhh, I don't know what to tell you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Very well, come on in. Perhaps I have something I can scald you with.
Spill it, Super-boss!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Very well... effective immediately the employee prescription drug program is terminated.
They're gonna win the championship, no thanks to me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait! You! Strawberry! Good effort today. Take a lap and hit the showers. I'm putting in a right-handed batter to hit for you.
Thanks, Mr. Burns. I owe it all to walking.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Walking, eh? Let me give it a try.
Huh?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We clashed lances on the Champs de Mars, and I have been bested. The plant is yours. Treat her well.
That worked sooo well.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We have several hours before the others arrive. What say we get comfy?
I wanna be back on the plane.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We'll be back before you know it.
But I can only sing lying on my back.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We'll cover it with a rewrite.
I think when we yelled we caused another avalanche.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We... should... be... careful... not... to... speak... unless... it's... absolutely... positively... necessary.
Apparently, old folks homes are full of people that used to be things. Just like you and me. Swear to God.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome, aficionados of the roped ring, to a thrilling night of senior-on-senior action.
Sure did.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome, come in. Ah, fresh victims for my ever-growing army of the undead.
I know.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well done, Monkey! That other panda gave some unexpected zazz to the festivities, eh?
Sure thing, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well done, Simpson. Now, walk behind me down the hallway.
I had no idea.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well in that case, just take us to whoever's in charge.
Uh, yes sir, Mr. Burns, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well then, get back to wherever it is you work, whoever you are.
Ow, ow! Oh, real mature, Lenny.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, Doc, I think I did pretty well on my tests. You may shake my hand if you like.
Yeah, he's funny.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I guess we'll have to relocate to an area where the workers are more desperate and ignorant. Springfield.
Wait a minute... because I brought the check, they named a wing after me? Oh, you must be mad.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I will be when the morphine wears off, but until then, Teedily deedily dee dee. Teedily dee dee dee. Woo hoo hoo. Hee hee hee.
And his arm can be my back-scratcher.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I've learned the robotic worker is no match for the old-fashioned man of labor. You're all hired back... as temps!
Don't mind if I do.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, Simpsie, you up for another wave?
You see, that's what I'm saying.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, a little do-re-mi will smooth this over.
Oooh, the the! But why are you helping me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, because before my wretched life comes to a close, I want to know that I had one friend. Also, because while you slept, I violated you repeatedly.
Oh, yeah! And I'm not easily impressed. Wow! A blue car!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, if a couple of Chinese bamboo gobblers can win people's hearts, I'm gonna bring them something that man has searched for since the dawn of time.
You just said it!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, if you liked that, listen to this: "Working hard... or hardly working?
That is the most amazing donut I've ever tasted.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, if you stay on at the Springfield Nuclear Plant, you could have one of these tasty beauties every day.
Sorry. Before we die, can you tell me how old you really are?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, it has four digits...
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, it looks like we've found this plant's one remaining worker of bone and sinew.
Mr. Burns, why'd you come to see me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, last night, I had a visit from three spirits...
At Lenny? But he's a war hero!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, let's decorate him then.
The rainforest?! That's that thing Lisa likes!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, maybe she'll like it better filled with dying trees and mutated animals.
Oh! Oh, yeah.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, now that I'm forcibly retired, I feel I should give back to society and do some charitable work. But first, I want to take a lot of opium.
And to make sure we get there super fast, I'm hitting all the buttons with my palm.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, that hurt like Hell.
Is that the trillion-dollar bill in his hand?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, that would be pretty careless of me, wouldn't it? I keep the real bill right here.
Really? How'm I doin'?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, well, if it isn't my favorite employee and his spouse. And these must be children. Have a ginger root.
I mean, screw you!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, well, it looks like my monkey has evolved into a man.
You remembered my name!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, who could forget the name of a magnetic individual like you? Keep up the good work, Max.
It's my first day.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, why didn't you say- Whoa! You're fired!
Oops! I thought this was the can, man.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, you're a Happy Homer. What's your name, young man?
Uh... yeah.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, you've won this round Simpson, but I'll grind you into the earth like a bug!
I worked for Fat Tony. And he was the best boss I ever had.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well. This is awkward.
Just give me a ticket.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well... all right, then. I don't want to seem like an ogre. I'll bide my time. Let him twist in the wind... slowly... slowly. And then... when the papers have found their new "flavor of the month", he'll find out this cat has claws!
Woo hoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What a disgraceful display. I've seen more orderly behavior in a Ritz Brothers film. You all need a serious lesson in teamwork.
Oh no.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What in blue blazes do you think you're doing, Simpson?
C'mon... Where are you... Here, Trilly, Trilly.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What is this? What are you doing?
Mr. Burns... I was wondering if I could get a raise.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What kind of a raise?
Oh. Well, thanks for your time.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What makes a man endanger his job, and yes, even his life, by asking me for money?
Uh, Mr. Burns, pirates got your yacht.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What!? Well, I suppose some mishaps are unavoidable.
Homer Simpson! Homer Simpson! Shut up! Homer Simpson! My name is Homer Simpson!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What? What are you talking about? Clearly make sense, man. I can't understand a word you're saying. You're just babbling incoherently like some sort of...
It's never good. I always wind up being chased by hounds, or falling through a trap door...or being a peg in your game of human croquet...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: When I made you a hoop you split your pants! Now here at the plant there's no position more important than our accounts man, who's responsible for glad-handing our customers and suppliers. I'd like you to take over that position.
Every time Mr. Burns has a birthday all his employees have to help out at the party. And I always get some terrible job.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Where is that dreaded piñata?
Good. Good. One more.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Where's my monster, Tubby? What do you people think I'm paying you for?
As Tolstoy said in "Quotable Notables," "Give me learning, sir, and you may keep your black bread.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who is that bookworm, Smithers?
You know what I think of this contract?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who is that firebrand, Smithers?
Drive to Chicago? I don't have time for that. I have to be back at work on Monday. And my boss is a total jerk.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who said anything about drive?
Hey, Burns! Eat my shorts!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who the Sam Hill was that?
Hey, I had a damn good reason. He could never remember my name...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who the devil are you?
I got the job. I got the job! Whoo hoo! Only in America could I get a job!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who was that young hellcat, Smithers?
You grandson-ruining fiend! Look what your "number one fan" did at show and tell!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who would film such a thing?
Well, nobody's perfect.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why can't the government just get off our backs?
All right, now you're startin' to creep me out.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why don't you just take my blood?
Got ya, Burnsie.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why you young ragamuffin. I was never one to back away from a snowball fight. Smithers, you may fire at will.
Mr. Burns, you brought us a present.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why, what did you think I was going to do -- have you beaten to a bloody pulp?
Why get up? Here's a little move I've been tinkering with. Say I want that bowl of dip.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why, you'd have to get up.
Hey, this isn't such a great prize. Oh, well, this may be a dirty job, but the big guys at the top work even harder.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Will five o'clock never come?
That's right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wrong. All beer trucks heading towards Springfield have been diverted. This town will be as dry as a bone. And if the rest of you beer swilling tube jockeys out there have a problem with this, talk to Homer Simpson.
Hello, Mr. Burns, this is the kidnapper. Do you miss your son?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes! I'm missing one son! Return it immediately!
Oh, Arthur Fortune!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes! That's the look I'm looking for. What would make you and your slovenly kind look at me that way?
A Lamborgotti Fasterossa? That's the car I think about when I make love to my wife.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, I need you to pick up my car at the factory in Italy, and ship it directly back to me. I'll save thousands in taxes!
Gee, it's not as nice as the other rooms.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, I really should stop ending the tour with it.
It's hard to believe there's a place worse than America, but we found it.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, I, too, feel renewed appreciation for the good old U.S. of A. Oppression and harassment are a small price to pay to live in the land of the free.
Look, Marge, I'm making a difference in people's lives!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, Simpson, your love of food is contagious.
Hmm... I'm just gonna put "haste makes waste.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, although these days I can make neither haste nor waste. You know, Simpson -- this has truly been a lovely afternoon.
But Mr. Burns, you're exhausted.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, but I have a little secret. I've obtained a rare, powerful aphrodisiac.
Mr. Burns, my son and I have been collecting coins. It's really brought us closer together. That penny you bought tonight would mean the world to him.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, but the problem is, if you had it, I wouldn't. You see the difficulty...
Well, you don't have to call me slovenly.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, exactly. That's the kind of pointer I need.
Are you sure you wanna do this so fast?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, my biological clock is ticking. I could be dead again soon.
That evil old bone bag... smelling of death... nose like a vulture... followed everywhere by that kiss-ass Smithers...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, that describes Kathy in Personnel to a tee!
Well, that loser Milhouse has always had a thing for her. Don't you love it when nerds don't know they're nerds?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, there's nothing more pathetic than self-delusion, eh.
Wow. You sure know how to cheat, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, I'm older than you. You know, Simpson, you're not as objectionable as you seemed when we first met.
Oh, man, you are so right. Did you ever sit like this?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes! That's it! Oh, I could go for one of those right now!
Plant-watering guy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, go ahead. And be careful with the Venus flytrap!
Hello!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, hello. Now, I need to find a patsy.
I think I won, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, you won all right. You won more than you bargained for.
Nice to meet you too, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. My attorneys have advised me to pay you for running over your child. So I'm cutting you a check.
Mr. Burns, are you trying to get me drunk?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. Now then, Homer, old chum, I'm sure you'll agree with me that this trial is an affront to our collective dignity. What do you say, we settle this man to man?
Joe DiMaggio?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes... it seems they've started letting ethnics into the big leagues.
Herb!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yess... that was Bonita De Wolf and the Springfield Nuclear Plant Soft Shoe Society.
Uh... uh yes, sir.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You and I are a dying breed, Simpson. I'm going to share something with you. Hop in.
Hello!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You bumbling fool, I keep telling you I'm looking for a patsy.
Hey, he's right...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You crooks in Washington have...
Comicon nerds!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You fool! These are robots! You will train them, and they will replace you.
I can't do this in front of Lisa. Why does she have to believe in things?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You have no choice. Pie him or I'll reveal your secret to the world!
I know.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know, Smithers, I think I'll donate a million dollars to the local orphanage... when pigs fly!
But you know what? To be loved you have to be nice to people. Every day! But, to be hated, you don't have to do squat.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You know, perhaps you're right. I got so swept up with the notion of being liked, I completely forgot who I am. I'm a selfish old crank and that fits me like a Speedo.
No, it's not. I just told a lie so we could go to Hawaii.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You lied to me! Release the hounds!
No! Mr. Burns, I'm not leaving until you say you're sorry for what you did to my wife.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You love her, too.
I can't do it, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You mean you're willing to give up a good job and a raise just for your principles?
Hey, you're not a penny.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You saved my life. There must be something I can do for you...
Wait a minute. Are you trying to get dirt on Lisa?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You saw right through me. Well done! Have some congratulatory drugs.
Mmm, open-faced club sand wedge...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're four strokes behind, Simpson.

Hmm. When you put it that way, it does sound a little far-fetched. But that's the lug you're looking at. And I vow to continue spending every free minute I have crusading for safety. Of course, I'd have a lot less of those free minutes if you gave me the job.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're not as stupid as you look... or sound... or our best testing indicates.
Hello!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're quite the friendly fellow, but right now I'm looking for a patsy.
The deal's off, Mr. Burns. The bear stays here.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You've made a mistake, Simpson.
Uh-oh. Wait a minute. Wait a minute. Stop the music... Quiet please... I have something to say. Quiet!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You, with the hair. Down in front!
Oh sorry, I wasn't listening. I was checking out my reflection in this yellow water. Lookin' good.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Young man, I have the answer to your problems.
Sweet dreams.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Young man, you have the noble bearing of the barbarian leader Vercingetorix
Mr. Burns, so glad you're here! Finally the party can get started!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Your cotillion seems to be in full promenade.
No, I was just up late watching a movie. Something with... William Holden and--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Your plan failed! Thank god this plant has never had a functioning air conditioner.
Yes, technically it's you. But like I said, people change and--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: --and they can also bloody well change back!
So, to contin-

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: -ue with the sad sto-
Well, despite all that, today's gonna be fun, Dad! Will there be lots of other girls there?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...after we show you the wealth of jobs in the steno pool, a hearty luncheon of bison with lake beaver will be served...
I want a photo of the hero who risked his life to save me!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: A picture of me with a smiling child?! I can get my plant back!
Mom, they're professional athletes. They're used to this sort of thing. It rolls right off their backs.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: All right, Monty, it's up to you managerial skills. What to do. Smithers, massage my brain.
I stand corrected.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: And now to present the award, here's former heavyweight champion, Smokin' Joe Frazier.
No! The computer says it's statistically impossible!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bah! Computers! They'll never replace my Huffnagle autocollator!
Mr. Smithers' father!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But I did not murder him.
Nooo!!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: But they're so wretchedly adorable! Twenty-five little Rory Calhouns. I can't do it!
But I need to prove that my ancestor couldn't have backed down to Colonel Burns!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Colonel Burns? Why, I haven't heard my father's name in years.
Mr. Burns, I came here because my brother is about to be wrongfully convicted. And the man I'm looking for would help me find the truth.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Don't you get it?! I don't care who you are or what you want.
Apparently not feisty enough. Future generations will judge us by how we cared for the tiniest creatures. I am not just asking you to save the bees. I am asking you to save your souls.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Excellent speech. Just excellent. I no longer wish to build my magnificent new basketball stadium.
...WALKING IN A WINTER WONDERLAND.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Exquisite, just exquisite. Makes me wish I hadn't released the hounds.
No, that's not it! A secret message this awkwardly-worded is always an anagram.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Fine. Then you unscramble those letters to spell out the location of the gem... while you two dig your own graves.
You want an alien? This is your alien!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello children! I bring you love!
But they're ours! You stole them from us!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Here's a phone. Call somebody who cares.
Dad! But if you're here, who's that on the float?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ho, ho, ho. Merry Fish-mas!
Stop! Don't shoot my Dad! He's innocent. He wouldn't hurt a fly!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ho-mer Simp... son. Ho... mersimp... son.
What's going on?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I call it the Burns Omni-Net. It sweeps the sea clean.
Oh, dear God!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I call our product: Li'l Lisa's Patented Animal Slurry! It's a high-protein feed for farm animals, insulation for low-income housing, a powerful explosive, and a top-notch engine coolant. And best of all, it's made from 100% recycled animals!
Mr. Burns, you can't do this!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I can, I shall and in the future I will have done. I cannot be stopped!
I propose to you that your heir need not be a boy. In this phallocentric society of ours...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't know what "phallocentric" means, but no girls.
Gimme that torch.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't see why I need a new driving license. My old one's just fine.
Ach! You haven't changed at all! You're still evil! And when you're trying to be good, you're even more evil!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I don't understand. Pigs need food, engines need coolant, dynamiters need dynamite. I'm supplying it to them, at a tidy profit, and not a single sea creature was wasted. You inspired it all, Li'l Lisa.
The Plywood Pelican was larger than a football field. It weighs more than the state of New Hampshire. It was only flown once, by its creator, Mr. C. Montgomery Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I flew it at an altitude of six feet for a distance of four-and-a-half feet. Then we discovered rain makes it catch fire. Then the Führer fired me.
Okay.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want you to weave that patented Simpson magic with my executives. A short speech, work work work, you know.
You again.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've realized the error of my ways, Lisa. I need someone with your integrity to help me. Please don't refuse this poor old man.
This whole building is just a façade for a drilling operation.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Indeed it is. "Evergreen Terrace" is built atop a massive shale deposit.
My name is Lisa, Mr. Burns. Lisa Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It doesn't matter what your name is, you idiot! What I want to know is: will you help me get my money back?
Whayda ya know, she's right.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It wasn't suppose to be this way. It was supposed to be a thing of beauty, not this abomination.
You're just a tiny ant, but you were strong enough to pull my brother and me together. Now go and be free.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Look, if I leave with you, they're just going to throw me back in.
I thought after all you went through, you just might want to spend an hour in a place where you felt at home.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Lots of room for friends.
Maybe you should wrap your hands behind your head.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Maybe I could wrap them around your gabby little throat!
I'm sorry Mr. Burns, but my paper's not for sale.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Maybe a little gift will change your mind.
I think it distracts people from more important social issues.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: My God, are you always on?
Maybe Mr. Smithers will help us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, he's out getting a spray-on tan. He comes back orange and stains the furniture -- the man's a walking creamsicle!
All right, it's all hooked up.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, it's all thanks to this self-powered experience approximater!
Oh... if I did agree to help you, you could only earn money by doing good, socially responsible things. Nothing evil.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nothing evil. That's exactly the kind of radical thinking I need! It's a deal.
Where am I gonna get five hundred dollars?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now drive, Smithers, drive!
No matter where you go... I will find you!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Nuclear energy was a craft before it was a science.
Hello. "We're here." "Hi." etc.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh goody, the Sea Monkeys I ordered have arrived. Look at them cavort and caper.
Dad, would you like some of my Snicker-bar cheesecake?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I feel full enough as it is.
Well, Mr. Burns, I hope you've realized the folly of killing innocent animals for fashion.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I have. I have! I swear I'll never wear any clothing made from an animal that can do an amusing trick!
I don't want to talk to you, Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I think you will. You see, I've just sold the Li'l Lisa Recycling Plant for 120 million dollars!
Mr. Burns! What are you doing here?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I've known about the gem for years. You see, my dear girl, I joined the Freemasons before it was trendy. That's my eyeball on the dollar bill.
I think I'm going to be sick...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, a spoonful of slurry will cure what ails ya!
Mr. Burns, if you want people to do a good job, you can't bully them. You have to show them they're appreciated.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, capital idea, partner. People, if we meet this week's quota, I'll take you to the most duck-filled pond you ever sat by.
He doesn't want your dirty money.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, come now. Everyone has his price.
Congratulations...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, don't congratulate me, congratulate Bay State Fish Sticks... as my advisor, you're entitled to ten percent of the proceeds.
Not good money, really. Each can'll get you a nickel.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, don't pooh-pooh a nickel, Lisa. A nickel will buy you a steak and kidney pie, a cup of coffee, a slice of cheesecake, and a newsreel! With enough change leftover to ride the trolley from Battery Park to the Polo Grounds.
Look -- there's writing on the "R!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, everything is "writing" to you young people!
It could be anything. It could be a mutant from the nuclear plant.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, fiddle-faddle. Everyone knows our mutants have flippers. Oops. I've said too much. Smithers, use the amnesia ray.
I'm so proud of you, Mr. Burns! You're getting your fortune back and you're doing it without endangering the planet or cozying up to the Aspen crowd.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, hold your accolades to the end of the tour. You haven't seen the best part!
Hmm. You've never heard of recycling? It means to reuse things to conserve our natural resources.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, so Mother Nature needs a favor? Well, maybe she should have thought of that when she was besetting us with droughts and floods and poison monkeys. Nature started the fight for survival and now she wants to quit because she's losing? Well, I say "hard cheese!
Well, at least it's tasteful.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, that's just a skip-rope rhyme. Believe me, the Lord's gonna go for this in a big way. Now, who's with me?
I understand. I'll just read a magazine.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Okay, here's the story: I belong to a very exclusive club -- The Excluders' Club...
Yes, sir. A very inane one. Mr. Burns, your campaign seems to have the momentum of a runaway freight train. Why are you so popular?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oooh, a tough question, but a fair one. Lisa, there's no single answer. Some voters respond to my integrity. Others are more impressed with my incorruptibility... still others by my determination to lower taxes, and the bureaucrats in the state capital can put that in their pipes and smoke it.
Mr. Burns, I hardly see what destroying our meager possessions is going to accomplish.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: She's right. Take me home, Smithers. We'll destroy something tasteful.
Congratulations, Isabel. I truly hope you enjoy the Friday morning council meetings and the, the free Snickerdoodle cookies.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! We won! Drop the balloons!
It looks great. I can't believe we scrubbed that old man smell out of a hundred and thirty-seven rooms.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, old chum, there's nothing like coming home with a clean bill of health. Oh, and sorry about your news.
Let's just pray this hits the prison.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, there's a rocket in my pocket.
Fine.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So ironic. After all my years of stock jobbing, gun running, attempted murder, successful murder, and tom peepery, they get me on a petty multi-million dollar art theft.
I can't. My Mom's not picking me up for an hour.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So... what do you think of today's popular music scene?
Um, I think we're supposed to get off here.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Take us out first! Anyone can start a family! These days, no one can find a job!
What do you mean you don't have anything to recycle? You must have some magazines, or newspapers.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That voice! That shrill, disagreeable voice! It's her!
Oh... on the radio.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's it, the radio! I'll go on the most popular program of the day. I assume that's still Don MacNeil and his Breakfast Club.
It's not fair!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's right, I pulled a Jesus. Have a nickel.
How did you find this?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The sheep was no danger at all. I sacrificed my gorgeous body for nothing. This must be what it's like to have a baby.
I'd love to -- Partner!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The whole plant is a environmentally-sound. It's powered by old newspapers. The machinery is made entirely of used cans. And the windows are from the old liquor bottles we collected.
He's giving them a bath!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: There you are, there ya go li'l' fella, and you...
Oh, it's beautiful.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This is an outrage! Since when are public figures fair game for satire?
They're so beautiful. And their breath smells like peppermint! No! No! I won't take your blood ponies! Go on, sweetie. Go on. Shoo!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Very well, you had your chance. I'm going to shred you like a Christmas card! Now, get out.
Just think what that game could do for Grampa and his friends!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait, I'm shooting at Nazis? That's not how I remember it.
Look! What's that?!!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We'll be dashed to pieces.
To that new stadium that looks exactly like a hive!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Welcome to the American dream: a billionaire using public funds to construct a private playground for the rich and powerful.
But nature's not our enemy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well surely you agree we can do without her.
Or from your point of view, M and S... Maggie Simpson.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What? No! With my last ounce of strength I sucked out my gold fillings and swallowed them. Those paramedics have sticky fingers.
You never let me tell!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Where are the hounds when I need them?
Mom, Dad! Mr. Burns is a vampire, and he has Bart!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Why Bart is right here.
You worked at Moe's?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes -- and therein lies a tale of woe and heartbreak. One I couldn't possibly recount.
Ha! I'd never help you. You're the worst man in the world.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes! That's the kind of moxie I'm looking for. You're hired!
Mr. Burns? Where's he going?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, I'd like thirty-seven snifters of your influenza syrup. One for me, one for Smithers here and the rest for my hounds.
Bart! That Pop Tart wasn't locally farmed or sourced!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You don't have a "whisper" voice, do you?
Oh, they've found a home.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You've won this round. But when next we meet, the beekeeper will be the beekeepee!
We've got to be realistic, kids. Who's gonna have a big enough heart to take care of twenty-five puppies?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...and I know the little fellas would love romping around my many acres, chasing my many cars, drinking from my many toilets...
Lisa, you're learning many lessons tonight and one of them is to always give your mother the benefit of the doubt.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...some can't even get a fair shake, or even a square deal... Ummmm, smells delightful.
Yay, Mom! All right, Mom!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...where our passions were inflamed by Clark Gable's reckless use of the word "damn.
Mr. Burns, you want to see me?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Actually, I was wondering if you were free for a little get-together tonight. Dinner, dancing and... Mr. Tom Jones.
That's odd. Where's Homer? And Bart? And Lisa? And Grampa?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: After all these years, things are finally starting to go my way. I feel like celebrating. I...
Well why can't I be greedy once in awhile?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bobo! My beautiful Bobo! I promise I'll never leave you behind again.
Mr. Burns seemed like such a nice man the day he arrived.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Cheap power, plentiful jobs, and all your swimming holes shall be warm and bubbling.
You were given six weeks to live. And you've outlived it! I think what kept you alive was that for once in your life you were helping other people.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Could it be? Perhaps kindness did keep me alive.
Why don't you publish your poem?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Don't I already give out turkey slices to the poor?
Okay, Homer. If you think I can.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Friends, art lovers, security personnel. Today is a red letter day for the Springfield Palace of Fine Art. A new wing for our museum and a portrait commemorating the man who ponied up the dough.
Is it Iraqi journalists being murdered?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Getting a little clingy, aren't we?
Homer, that was Apollo Twelve!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Greetings, wage-donkeys. Is everyone happy and content?
Oh, my! It's Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Heave-ho! Heave-ho! Heave-ho! Heave-ho! Heave-ho!
The one what?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hello, Smithers. Nice of you to drop by... after my life was saved.
Well, maybe not, but I have the gift of being able to see inner beauty.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmmm. Mrs. Simpson, you may immortalize me.
Mr. Burns, isn't it more important that you got a child to smile at you?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Honestly no, I'd rather have the gold.
That's what I said, foilage. It doesn't take a nucular scientist to pronounce foilage.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Honestly, Smithers, I don't know why Harvard even bothers to show up. Heh. They barely even won.
Yours, Homie. I'm always on yours.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: How ironic. I survived the Titanic by making a raft out of steerage passengers and now this!
Well, I'm just relieved that Homer's safe and you've recovered and we can all get back to normal. If Maggie could talk I'm sure she'd apologize for shooting you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I' afraid that's insufficient. Officer, arrest the baby.
I guess no one gives a damn about the American family anymore.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll sign your petition!
I don't think that will be a problem.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'm no matinee idol.
Oh, my.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: If you'll excuse me, I'm changing for a board meeting.
Oh, and how about piping in some Tom Jones music? That always cheers me up.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: It's working! It's working! And the healthy snacks are on their way.
That's wonderful Homer, I'm so proud of...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Let me get this straight. You're pleased with your current appearance? Ah, why my good man, you're the fattest thing I've ever seen. And I've been on safari.
We don't need TV to have family fun. Why don't we play Monopoly?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Let's get started. First I'd like to announce that thanks to the magic of Disney Animatronics, Strom Thurmond will live another hundred years.
How clever! The kids' menu's on the beak.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Mm, I think I'll take... Ooh, that one.
Mr. Burns!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No need for alarm. I just came to give you the orchids and fragrant bath oils I lavish upon all my employees.
He's not dead.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, but his career is. I remember when Al Jolson ran amok at the Winter Garden and climbed the Chrysler Building. After that, he couldn't get arrested in this town.
Well, I'm just relieved that Homer's safe and you're recovered and we can all get back to normal.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not exactly. Smithers, for attempting to kill me, I'm giving you a five percent pay cut.
Marge!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, I insist you take off your shoes when you get inside. And uh, while you're in there, grab as much cancer as you can.
You keep your hands to yourself, mister.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, we don't want to kill him, shoot him around the groin and belly.
Well, I don't like this movie. And I'm going to boycott your financier... Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh really? And what will you use instead of nuclear power?
I didn't know you liked animals.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, I don't like everything about them, just their heads. Well, would you care for some wine, old buddy?
All I wanted to do was join a group of women who wore the same outfits.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, no jury on earth will convict a bunch of moist-eyed mothers. I'll tell you what, ladies, give me my eggs back and I'll let you go.
Should we take all our stuff, or are we coming back on this boat too?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Same boat, but uh, take it anyway. They use the boat for a Dixieland Booze Cruise while we're gone.
Homer, please pay attention. There's just one more movie.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simple villagers, I promise you I will close plants in America and bring work here.
Take off the 3-D glasses!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson! A gangly little bird told me you've been lollygagging at the Biograph.
What a delightful sprite.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! There seems to be some sort of communiqué on that man's blouse.
I wish I'd pay more attention.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, this beer isn't working. I don't feel any younger or "funkier.
Oh, well, isn't that... Whoa!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, this is a golden opportunity. If we get him alive we can put him on Broadway. Dead, we'll sell monkey stew to the Army!
Or, or, um, with, with a funny hat on.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So profit margins will be thinner than Louise Brooks' negligee.
You're gonna get a bath tonight.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So the good news is, church revenues are up one thousand and seventy-three percent.
A formal. The one place you can wear a tiara and not look crazy.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, how are we enjoying the festivities?
Okay. One night.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, let's see how my burly-bottomed ball-handlers are faring. Smithers, we're leading two to nothing! Run out the clock, boys. Run out the clock...
Aww. He can crawl up through my toilet any day.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, tell me, are all you government inspectors so handsome and strapping?
Milhouse?!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Sure, handmade electricity costs more and powers less... but maybe that's the point.
Mr. Burns, I've had enough of your... posing. I can finish the portrait myself.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Thank goodness. Another day in this suburban nightmare and I would've needed half a white valium. Thank you for your gracious hospitality. See you at the unveiling.
Come home soon.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That's it. That's it. Come closer...
I don't know. Maybe we should take his money and put all this ugliness behind us.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The fish is in the pan.
What's he saying?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Uh, he's saying, "We wouldn't dream of sacrificing the blue-haired woman!
Goodness!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Up-up-up-up. Don't answer me now. Relax, talk it over with the missus, soak in the opulence of your surroundings and dream of what might be. Smithers, let's go powder my nose.
Homer, please. No one's going to notice if you wear a pink shirt to work.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Wait a minute, go back. Zoom in. Why is that man in pink?
Bart!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We'll have you out of there as soon as our tech boys get you decontaminated.
Mr. Burns, it's hard to discover your inner beauty while you're shouting at an eight-year-old girl.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: We've only got two days left, so I'd advise you to shut up and paint!
Whatever it does, it's doing it now.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I'll let you get acquainted with Señor Xt'tapalatakettle. Ta!
What were you like as a boy, Mr. Burns? Did you have a dog that you loved.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, aieeee! There's something on my leg! Get it off! Get it off!
Single white female wanted for mysterious expedition. Must like monkeys. Non-smoker preferred.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, you'd be a welcome change of pace from the rest of these crude and uncouth sailors.
Oh... well, yeah, the ointments, um...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What are you people doing in my summer home?
You always do the right thing... sort of.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What is he doing? He was furious at that woman, now he's embracing her. He told me himself they had nothing in common!
Mr. Burns, you can't hurt us after all we've done for you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What the devil are you talking about?
Oh, I don't think Mr. Burns would like that show.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: What's the matter? Think I'm not hip? I don't have enough vo-dee-oh-doh?
Mr. Burns? You care about children?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, particularly their supple young organs. Oh unfenced back yard pools, where would I be without you?
See!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, thank you, everyone. But -- 10% of your applause should go to my little partner, Lisa Simpson. For if it were not for her infectious moralizing, we would not be here today to witness the unveiling of... The Li'l Lisa Recycling Plant!
Oh, am I in the way?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, yes, you're in the way! Are you daft, woman?
Uh-huh. The Fire Department.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes. They're new, but they're good.
You can't fire me just because I'm married. I'm going to sue the pants off you.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You don't have to sue me to get my pants off.
Mr. Burns, how can you be so cold- hearted?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You have no idea, woman, what that man's put me through.
Well, you could give them healthier snacks... theme days...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You mean like "Child labor Day"?
My husband will be so excited.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You... have a husband? Yes, I can picture him now... rugged good looks... sweater knotted about his shoulders... curly locks shining in the sun like spun gold...
Okay, everybody tuck your pants into your socks.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...and the bold, new ideas these tiny tykes unveil for us today could make thousands of jobs like yours obsolete!
If I couldn't spend the treasure on Edner, I didn't want to spend it. I just sat there playin' our song on the jukebox. One gold--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: ...coin at a time.
He's a pip, this one is!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ah, the mirthless laugh of the damned. Hold your nose, Smithers, we're going in!
Hey, hey, ya mugs. Thinkin' ain't drinkin'!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bring that girl to me.
Hey guys, uh, you'll need this on your trip to Hawa--

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hm, your goblin fainted.
Hey! If you guys are getting loaded off them fumes, I'm gonna have to charge ya.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I want that oil well! I've got a monopoly to maintain! I own the Electric Company and the Waterworks, plus the hotel on Baltic Avenue.
Well, if you own a bar, you either keep it clean or learn to deal with inspectors. And Moe don't clean.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Interesting attitude for a janitor. What say we make you the new supervisor of Sector 7-G?!
That's right, she's into puppets.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Just what's going on here?
Can you blame him?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No, no I can't.
God, misfire!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Now, I'd like to introduce you to your new manager. You'll find his integrity and dedication make him untouchable.

Oh, so you're looking for a Mr. Smithers, eh? First name, Waylon, is it? Listen to me, you... when I catch you, I'm going to pull out your eyes and shove 'em up your pants so you can watch me kick the crap out of you. Okay? Then I'm going to use your tongue to paint my boat.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oh, Smithers, if only you could hear me.
Thank you for your time.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: One hundred thousand dollars.
Not a goblin.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Simpson! Where's your Christmas tree?
Take that!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers! That precision assault popped it back into place! Thank you masked stranger!
Don't worry about nothin', Homer. I have a feeling that Mr. Burns is gonna have a little accident that might keep him from bowling with us tonight. Heh, heh, heh...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, I'm afraid I won't be able to play tonight. My old gimpy knee has gone akimbo again, and...
Well as supervisor, I can't fraternize with the... uh... what's the word... scum. Anyway, because I am your friend, you are safe. But you're gonna be reassigned.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Smithers, what profit a man if he gain the world and lose his soul. Seriously. I need an amount. In round dollars.
Goodnight eggs. Goodnight dregs. Goodnight bugs crawlin' up my legs. Goodnight beer. Goodnight mice. Goodnight Princess who treats me nice. Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So my offer... for one ton of your uranium... is a goat.
Just jump!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: So, I see by your tie you're a Yale man, too. Let's croon, shall we? BOOLA BOOLA / BOOLA BOOLA...
Ah, that kid slays me.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: That was no accident. Let's get out of here.
A mix of conservation and wind.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Who told you about those?
Aw, ain't that cute? Makes Li'l Debbie look like a pile of puke!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Would you like to be the first to take a tour of the plant, Li'l Lisa?
Oh God, here it comes -- time-share pitch. Well I got bad credit, so the joke's on you!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: You're here to participate in a hunt for the world's most dangerous game.
How much to have Bart crank-call me? That would be hilarious. Eh, that's just me, though. You know, I love to laugh.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Young man, I believe you have something that belongs to me.
Hi fellow Halloweenies! Did I scaredly-dare ya?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ladies and gentlemen, in his native land he was a king. But he comes before you in chains, for your own amusement. Presenting Homer, the Eighth Wonder of the World!
Now, there's no need to actually whip 'em. We can put the sound in later.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: No! As your financial backer, I insist upon reality. Pharaoh didn't put the sound in later!
Well, this goes right into the old poor box.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Not so fast, old chum.
One hundred and one thousand!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Pass. I've already lifted this thing once today. I'm not Hercules!
Howdy gents. What can I diddily do you for?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Remember, Smithers. In and out in eighteen seconds.
Hey there, Mr. Burns! For our half hour I thought we'd have a picnic in the park.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Silence, you sadistic monster! I've got my memory back, and I'm going to wreak a terrible vengeance. Taking an idea I got from a Stephen King book, I'm going to cover this town with a dome!
But who'd know the difference?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: The people being whipped!
Homer! Gimme back my tree!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, I won't interrupt your holiday any longer. Merry Christmas to all and to all a good... pop star slash fashionista, Katy Perry?!
... So recycling is our way of giving Mother Earth a great big hug.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, well, it does sound like fun. I can't wait to start pawing through my garbage like some starving raccoon.
That's odd. I don't have a secretary, or an intercom. But send him in.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Ahoy there, Dean! I understand you're taking suggestions from students, eh? Well, me and my Fourth Form chums think it would be quite "corking" if you'd sign over your oil well to the local energy concern!
Well, I'm going to take advantage of this rare opportunity, even if you children aren't interested. Uh... Which do you think is more important: hard work or stick-to-it-iveness?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Are there any real questions?
Thank you, Superdude.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Bah! A non-profit organization with oil? I won't allow it! An oil well doesn't belong in the hands of Betsy Bleedingheart and Maynard G. Muskie-vote!
The holiday season is approaching and these children need a school...

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Charity, eh? Yes, I'd be more than happy to...
Finally, in nineteen ninety-two, I was reunited with that chair. It wasn't quite the same.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Good God, I'm at war with a little girl... and I'm losing!
We could make it if we took Mr. Burns's helicopter.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Hmm... I don't really want you people inside, but you could dangle from the skids.
That hotel's a dump, and your monopoly is pathetic. The school's oil well is not for sale. Particularly to a black-hearted scoundrel like yourself!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I see. Then I'll just have to... AT-TTACK YOU!
Super. Now, let's give a big Junior Achievers welcome to our guest speaker -- I know he can teach us a lot about business -- Mr. C. Montgomery Burns!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I'll keep it short and sweet. Family, religion, friendship: these are the three demons you must slay if you wish to succeed in business. When opportunity knocks, you don't want to be driving to the maternity hospital or sitting in some phony baloney church. Or synagogue. Questions?
Monty Burns, everybody!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: I've called you all here because I need some honest answers. What is my current financial situation?
Hmm... Oh. I'm going to have to think about that. Meanwhile, wear this home.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Oooo... I need some more ether. I can still feel the movement of the emery board.
In order to save money, the following presidents will no longer be taught: Buchanan, Fillmore, Pierce, Bush, Bush... could you please stop that?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Saratoga slam! Aristotle's dilemma! Knickerbocker knucklebreaker! And so on.
Aaaaaand freeze! Now, who in Springfield will eat the poisoned broth? Whoo, it could be anyone, even Mr. Burns.

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: This play really speaks to me.
Oh, the word "ring!

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Well, well. If it isn't the Tardy Boys and Nancy Clueless.
Who?

dialogue.speaker: C. Montgomery Burns
dialogue.text: Yes, I regained consciousness during my big dance number. Those strings pulling me every which way jostled my heart from its slumber.
